#4535. Lando Norris Extends São Paulo Pole Streak Ahead of Brazilian Grand Prix

Norris will start the Brazilian Grand Prix from pole position for the third straight year as George Russell furiously misses out on pole before grid penalty.

Lando Norris secured his 20th career pole the weekend after he officially passed on the championship title to Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli will join Norris on the front row, qualifying third and moving up a spot after his teammate George Russell received a grid penalty.

Russell, who was fastest in Q2 and fastest through sectors 1 and 2 in the final qualifying session as well, was told to back off on his final lap as the rain, which plagued the entire qualifying, picked up again. Russell was running up on Alex Albon’s Williams also in a flying lap and radioed for his former teammate to move out of the way. He was then called back potential in hopes of staying out for another out lap and hitting his second flyer on a wet but clearer track.

Furious over the radio to his race engineer, Marcus Dudley, Russell raged about being called off. Russell’s provisional pole of 1:27.674 was beaten by Norris by 0.204 seconds on the 2025 Drivers' Champion's second lap, and the English Mercedes driver was convinced that his next lap would be a step better.

“Mate! Russell yelled. “You told me to back off. What the hell?”

“George, you’re P2,” Toto Wolff replied over the radio.

With six minutes to go in the final stage, Russell was called to the garage and told to stay in the car just in case they could get out for a final out lap and flying lap. Dejected, his qualifying ended here, and his starting position moved from second to seventh with his five-place grid penalty.

I’m P2, but I don’t want to be P2; I want to be P1,” Russell radioed again.

While the difference between a sixth and seventh place start at Sao Paulo is small, Russell felt cheated out of a pole, which would still be recorded even with his grid penalty.

“Yeah, I mean, obviously congrats to Lando, but yeah, that was definitely the pole lap,” Russell said. “Misjudgment on our side; we need to understand what happened. Obviously, the rain was coming, and we should have just finished the lap.”

Leclerc qualified fourth and will start third next to Liam Lawson who was second fastest in Q2 and held provisional pole early in Q3. Lawson, who is not confirmed to have a seat with Racing Bulls or elsewhere next year, had his best qualifying in fifth. His best of the year at both Red Bull and Racing Bulls has been eighth, twice.

Nico Hulkenberg qualified sixth and will start sixth, and Isack Hadjar is the final driver upgraded with Russell’s penalty. Haas’ Oliver Bearman will start eighth, and Fernando Alonso and Alex Albon both made their first Q3 appearances of the year and will start ninth and tenth, respectively.

#4534. Zoomlion says its new, 1,600 hp hybrid tractor is the world’s most powerful

Chinese equipment brand Zoomlion showed up to this week’s China International Agricultural Machinery Exhibition with a new ultra-high-horsepower hybrid tractor that sets a new benchmark, offering more than 1,600 hp while cutting back on both fuel and fumes.

Zoomlion calls its new 9DX hybrid tractor a radical rethink of what a modern ag unit can be, combining the all-day pulling power of a conventional diesel machine with the efficiency, accuracy, and instant torque benefits of electric drive. The company claims its hybrid setup can reducing fuel consumption, emissions, and deliver lower operating costs, without asking massive industrial farming operations to walk away from diesel entirely.

The tractor itself gets a headline-grabbing 1,600 hp Zoomlion 9DX features an 800V hybrid electric powertrain and continuously variable transmission that delivering a peak torque of 7,200 Nm (~5,300 lb-ft) of torque. Getting all that power to the ground is a four track tank-drive system riding on Zoomlion’s in-house developed 762 mm (~30 inch) wide tracks that are designed to distribute the tractor’s considerable weight for maximum traction and minimum soil compaction. What’s more, the high-traction treads can push the big machine to hit a maximum speed of 40 km/h across grades and slopes of up to 12 degrees.

The 9DX also gets a high-capacity hydraulic system capable of delivering 636 liters per minute of flow (~170 GPM), allowing it to work with some seriously heavy duty implements like ultra-wide seeders and variable-rate fertilizer applicators.

The Zoomlion 9DX was one of several new machines at this year’s exhibition, which hosted more than 3,000 exhibitors and vendors – but the big hp numbers all over the show made an even bigger impression, leading AGCO’s director of global electronic and electrical engineering, Nicolas Meunier, to tell Chinese State news agency Xinhua that the country had moved on from producing mostly low-horsepower tractors to building some seriously large machines.

There’s no official word on specs and batteries, but the company has developed an 800V modular battery pack system for its other equipment offerings that can scale from 140-800 kWh of capacity while other top-shelf Zoomlion tractors featuring an ag version of Cummins’ 15 liter turbodiesel.

The 9DX tops off what’s sure to be another record year for Zoomlion, which is coming off strong early export quarters shipping into Germany, Australia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

#4533. Tesla Sold FSD To Koreans Who Still Can't Use It. Now It's Facing A Complaint

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Tesla's Full Self-Driving will turn 10 years old next month. Nearly four of those years have labeled FSD as an official beta product, and over two additional years have been under the new "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" rebranding. Whatever the name, the car that is in your driveway today still can't technically drive itself without you being responsible for what happens behind the wheel.

Needless to say, some drivers are getting impatient—especially those who have purchased FSD for multiple cars, or have managed to pay off their car loan before getting unsupervised FSD. Now a consumer advocacy group in South Korea is firing back to demand answers and accountability.

The rollout of FSD in Korea is even more confusing that it is in the U.S. thanks to another layer of complexity: where the vehicle was manufactured.

According to Reuters, only about 20% of the Teslas registered in South Korea—vehicles assembled in the United States—are actually eligible to enable the Full Self-Driving software. That's because those vehicles meet the U.S. Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards, and a trade agreement with the U.S. designates those standards as acceptable to enter Korea without additional modification.

The majority of the remaining vehicles have been manufactured in China, where no agreement (or supplementary safety certification) for its FSD software exists today. Since 2023, Tesla has imported about 170,000 of these Shanghai-built cars with the volume of Chinese-built cars increasing five-fold last year alone. In fact, 99% of Teslas imported into China in 2025 were from China and ineligible to activate FSD.

A complaint being filed by Korean consumer advocacy group Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty (reviewed by Reuters) with the Korean Fair Trade Commission alleges that Tesla has still been collecting money from buyers for its FSD software for over three years, despite the software not being available to buyers due to this restriction. This meant buyers forked over as much as $6,800 for the feature, but haven't actually been able to switch it on. Some buyers instead resorted to enabling region-locked FSD via a "jailbreak," which is seen as a safety circumvention and led to owners facing jail time or fines of up to $15,000.

Things get a bit more complicated given the recent legal loss raised by dozens of Tesla owners who had their lawsuit thrown out of Korean courts just last week. According to the ruling from the Seoul Central District Court, Tesla didn't technically break its contractual obligations with the 88 owners who requested full refunds via a lawsuit filed in 2024.

The court acknowledged that Tesla's delivery of the features promised with FSD hinged on certain technical advances and regulatory approval that buyers were aware could "take considerable time to become available," according to reporting by the South China Morning Post. If those didn't happen, the court says that Tesla isn't in the wrong.

The complaint by Citizens United raises additional questions about the way that Tesla advertises its vehicles to consumers. And they're not the first. The KFTC confirmed to Reuters that it launched a probe into Tesla's advertising earlier this year, but declined to comment further. Tesla didn't respond to the outlet's request for comment.

Whether or not this avenue will result in action after the court's ruling that buyers weren't entitled to a refund is unclear.

#4532. Buick Electra GS Is a Sleek New Plug-In Hybrid Sedan for China

Designed for the Chinese market, the Electra GS looks significantly different than the concept shown last year, with sharp, C-shaped LED headlights.

While there are reports of a new sedan on the horizon, Buick’s lineup in the United States currently only consists of SUVs. But over in China, Buick offers a healthy arsenal of sedans, from the compact Verano to the larger LaCrosse. Now Buick is about to introduce a new electrified sedan called the Electra GS, and the first images of the new car have been leaked via China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT).

The MIIT periodically publishes information on upcoming automotive products, and the official filing is the first time we’ve seen the final production design for the Electra GS, which was first previewed by a concept in 2025. Confusingly, Buick already offers a sedan called the Electra L7 in China, sold with electric and range-extender plug-in hybrid powertrains, but the new Electra GS seems poised to be a less potent and more affordable option.

See all results for used Buick for sale near 33913

The new Electra GS is a bit smaller than the Electra L7, measuring 196.0 inches from nose to tail, just over two inches shy of the L7. The GS is also 1.5 inches narrower and has a 5.3-inch shorter wheelbase than the L7. Under the hood, the Electra GS will employ a plug-in hybrid setup that uses either a 97-hp naturally aspirated 1.5-liter inline-four or a turbocharged 1.5-liter making 154 hp. The gas engines are paired with an electric motor producing 221 horsepower, which feeds off a lithium iron phosphate battery.

Stylistically, the production Electra GS is a significant departure from the concept, with a more traditional sedan shape than the concept’s taller, hatchback look. The front end has thin headlights that wrap around a trim piece that stretches across the front and can be either body colored or finished in silver. The Electra GS has a fastback roofline and smooth surfacing, while the taillights span the width of the vehicle before curving inward.

Overall, the Electra GS looks smart and modern, and Buick will hope that the GS can help reverse its sales slide in China. The Electra GS won’t be coming to the U.S., but it could give a sense of Buick’s future styling direction that could appear on the rumored gas-powered sedan expected to arrive in the next couple of years.

#4531. Liebherr expands excavator range with new, 250-tonne electric model

It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little, but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.

Liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024, and electric power has proven to be effective – moving millions of tons of dirt while saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs. Now, the company is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a new, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.

Based on the proven R 9300 G8 platform, the new Liebherr R 9300 G8-E packs an 850 kW (~1,140 hp) electric drivetrain designed to IEC standards and supports 6-6.6 kV power supplies. The company says its electric setup offers customers the same hydraulic power and bucket capacity (1.8 tonnes/cubic meter, or ~1.5 short tons/cubic yard) as the diesel version.

All that electric power ships with advanced electronics and operator assistance systems designed to maximize both efficiency and safety while giving mine operators more data to work and plan with. Liebherr describes its take on ADAS thusly:

The R 9300 G8-E comes with Liebherr Power Efficiency – Hydraulic Control as standard, which adapts hydraulic power to suit the machine’s load profile, reducing overall engine load factor. Thanks to its Generation 8 electronic architecture, the R 9300 G8-E is compatible with a range of Liebherr’s IoMine technology products, including its range of excavator Assistance Systems, the semi-autonomous Bucket Filling Assistant, the Skyview vision system as well as the data visualisation tool, Data View. Customers also have the option of installing Liebherr’s autonomous cable reel solution onto the excavator to assist with cable management and support machine mobility on site.

Like its repowered cousins, the big electric excavator does seem to have on-board batteries, but is primarily driven and operated with grid power, reducing charging and re-charging concerns and enabling round-the-clock operations for as long as grid power holds.

Liebherr touts the benefits of new R 9300 G8-E’s quiet, emissions-free running throughout its official announcement, but doesn’t stop there. The company says its EV, which makes do with thousands of fewer moving parts in its drivetrain, can also reduce maintenance requirements and associated operating costs in certain applications and site conditions while improving workplace conditions for the people who work in and around the machine.

Operating electric machinery inside mines must be mindblowingly good. Location is quite fixed, so you can just lay a HV cable to the grid with a spool at the vehicle end for local mobility. No noise, no vibration, no dirty emissions that have to be ventilated out for you not to die, instant torque, massive power and less maintenance on top?

The electric drivetrain also reduces vibration inside the cab, improving operator comfort, limiting fatigue, and potentially contributing to a safer working environment.

#4530. The 2027 Chevy Silverado EV Gets A Power Bump And A NACS Port

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Chevrolet is giving its most expensive electric pickup a power bump for the 2027 model, not that it needed it. The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss with the Max Range battery pack now puts down a whopping 750 horsepower and 775 pound-feet of torque, as reported by GM Authority.

That’s 25 hp more than the outgoing model, but it’s worth noting that the maximum output is only available when activating the Wide Open Watts (WOW) mode, which pushes every metric to the top for maximum acceleration, but isn’t intended for regular use. Chevrolet doesn’t say how much power the Silverado EV makes when the WOW mode is disabled.

The power figures of all other Silverado EV trims stay the same, but as with all 2027 General Motors EVs, they now come from the factory with a native Tesla-style NACS charging port. This enables them to pull up to Tesla Superchargers and other NACS-equipped chargers and top up without needing an adapter.

For 2027, the electric pickup also gains a few new cameras. The Cabin Glance feature shows a live video feed of the car’s interior on the infotainment screen. Then, there’s Security Recording, which records video from the vehicle’s on-board cameras when the alarm is triggered. Last but not least, the Surround Vision Recorder acts as an on-board video security system that continuously records footage while the car is in use, much like Tesla’s Dashcam feature.

The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado EV is slightly more expensive than the outgoing model on all trims. The base Silverado EV Standard Range starts at $56,085 (including destination charges), $700 more than the previous model. Meanwhile, the LT and Trail Boss trims with the Extended Range battery are now $1,000 more than last year, while the top-spec Trail Boss with the Max Range battery now starts at $90,395, or $1,200 more than the 2026 model.

All Silverado EV trims come with a dual-motor, all-wheel-drive setup. The entry-level WT trim has 510 hp and 490 or 580 lb-ft of torque, depending on the battery capacity. The LT Standard Range gets 605 hp and 605 lb-ft of torque, followed by the LT Extended Range, with 645 hp and 765 lb-ft of torque. The Trail Boss Extended Range has 625 hp and 775 lb-ft of torque, and the Trail Boss Max Range pushes the power figure up to 750 hp.

Besides more power and torque, the Trail Boss also comes with a two-inch suspension lift, a more aggressive off-road body kit, 35-inch tires, four-wheel steering as standard, and some new driving modes. Despite the trail-oriented kit, the Trail Boss is the longest-range model in the lineup, with up to 478 miles on the Max Range battery.

The RST trim, which used to be the top option, has been discontinued. Production of the 2027 Chevy Silverado EV kicked off at GM’s Factory Zero in Michigan last month.

Every TX rolls off the assembly line with a suite of driver-assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, and more.

#4528. Gray Zone Warfare Update Addresses Biggest Rogue Ops Concerns

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

Gray Zone Warfare stands out for its immersion as a PvE open-world tactical shooter set on a quarantined Southeast Asian island with plenty of narrative elements to get stuck into. Rogue Ops allows for a fresh experience by building your very own Hideout and growing your reputation in new ways.

The ambitious mode has a lot to love, but it has faced its fair share of player complaints, as major issues have been interrupting the fun in the gameplay loop. A Halloween Dev Stream teased significant improvements to enemy AI and making the Hideout economy more rewarding.

This is the detailed all purpose hub for Gray Zone Warfare guides and content.

Now that Gray Zone Warfare Patch 0.5.1.0 is live, we can dive into all the key changes you can expect to see when you embark on your next mission.

First of all, huge changes have been made to the way enemy AI behaves. One of the biggest criticisms players had of the AI enemies was their inconsistency and the feeling of them being extremely overpowered.

Following this update, enemies should no longer know your exact position after shooting. Sound now only gives them an approximate location, meaning the farther away you are, the more difficult it is for them to detect you. Rather than the AI instantly sharing your exact position, they'll rely on information they can gather, which ultimately makes their reactions more natural.

Stealth has also undergone some work to make it more consistent. Moving slowly should make you harder to detect, and the AI exhibits reactions to light that you’d expect. These changes should make stealth, flanking enemies, and repositioning more rewarding and allow you to take a greater advantage over your surroundings.

Improvements have also been made to how enemies engage in combat. Trained soldiers bring more precision to their combat abilities and make better use of cover, but untrained enemies will be more careless in their actions.

Combined with fixing pesky problems with hit boxes, grenades, and enemies getting stuck behind doors, this series of changes aims to make combat more varied and test your tactical performance.

Sound now only gives them an approximate location, meaning the farther away you are, the more difficult it is for them to detect you.

Another major change has been made to the economy in Hideout. A range of rewards have been increased, including raising the rewards from smuggling tasks and increasing the sales prices of smuggling backpacks, and improving rewards from hideout handovers and increasing the sale prices of hideout products.

Production and disassembly times have even been reduced across the board, and the size and weight of selected building materials and disassembly have been reduced for a better looting experience.

The Gray Zone Warfare update arrives with a slew of bug fixes to gameplay, animations, audio, tasks, and so much more. This includes fixing a bug where the health panel could show 100% damage on an organ that was not destroyed and repairing an issue that caused some tasks to not be offered due to a nearby task blocking them. The full patch notes can be viewed here.

In the meantime, the team will continue to address further feedback, like AI enemies seemingly taking too many shots to kill, provided as an example, with further fixes planned for upcoming patches. The developers are already working on their next major update, Patch 0.5.2.0.

#4527. Lucid teases its cheaper sub-$50,000 Cosmos EV in new video and images

Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.

The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.

Lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video on X yesterday. The caption talks about “elevating the experience of movement” and says Lucid can’t wait “to share this feeling with even more people.” It doesn’t name the vehicle, but “even more people” is about as subtle a hint at a cheaper model as you can get.

Two frames from the film show the vehicle at dusk. At the rear, “LUCID” is spelled out in red illuminated letters across the tailgate, flanked by thin red light strips, with a spoiler cutting across the base of the rear glass. Up front, a sculpted LED headlight with a row of vertical segments sweeps across a red body panel.

That rear end matches the Cosmos design Lucid registered with the EU Intellectual Property Office in May, which showed the same spelled-out “LUCID” tailgate and rear-glass spoiler. It also lines up with the thin red light strips on the camouflaged Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101 in California last month.

Lucid unveiled its plans for Cosmos and Earth at its first Investor Day in March. Both ride on the new midsize platform and start under $50,000, roughly half the price of the Gravity.

On paper, the Cosmos is impressive. Lucid claims about 300 miles of range from a 69 kWh pack, thanks to efficiency of up to 4.5 mi/kWh, which it says is 10% better than its closest competitor. It also claims 200 miles of range in 14 minutes of charging, and its new Atlas drive unit has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the Zeus unit in the Gravity.

The problem is timing. Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, CEO Silvio Napoli pushed the Cosmos to 2027, “most likely the second half.”

That puts it on the same schedule as Rivian’s $45,000 base R2, and well after the Tesla Model Y it was caught testing next to in Arizona back in May.

Lucid needs this car badly. It delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while building only 2,954 after cutting the second shift at its Arizona factory.

I want Lucid to succeed. Period. I love the Air Pure and would like to get one at some point, but the cost is out of my budget while the tech is more than I want or need.

But I think what impresses me more than anything with Lucid is that they are one of the few who actually speak efficiency. It seems that they actually care about being efficient where companies like GM and others just build vehicles with bigger batteries in order to get more range. So for that, I give Lucid much credit.

The company is building hype a year out. It has nothing else new to sell until the Cosmos arrives, and the company reports Q3 earnings on Monday. They need to remind everyone what they are working toward.

A midsize SUV doing 4.5 mi/kWh would be best in class by a wide margin, and Lucid’s efficiency claims have held up on the Air. If it really lands under $50,000 with 300 miles of range, it’s a very compelling alternative to the Model Y and the R2, which still have room to take over market shares from ICE vehicles.

But Lucid has already slipped this car once; it says its cash lasts “well into 2027,” and the Cosmos is due in the second half of 2027. That’s a tight overlap. I think the Cosmos will be a good car, but can Lucid fund it all the way to customers’ driveways?

#4526. This Startup Wants To Turn Teslas Into Anything, From 11-Seat Minibuses To Pickups

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The slightly dorky vehicle you see here can use Tesla’s Superchargers and so-called Full-Self Driving (Supervised) driver assistance system. And no, your eyes are not deceiving you—this is not a Tesla. At least, not at first glance.

It’s called the Hoffman Badger, and it’s the creation of a small Wisconsin startup that wants to turn old Tesla EVs into pretty much any type of vehicle. The first Badger made its debut at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas, driving on its own wheels all the way from its home base and using Superchargers along the way, just like any Tesla would.

Hoffman says it uses all of the hardware and software from the donor vehicle, which can be either the Model 3 or Model Y. The seats, dashboard, steering wheel, motors, and even the door handles are lifted from Tesla. Then, they’re installed in a new chassis that puts the high-voltage battery pack one and a half inches higher than in the original vehicles. This, along with the eight-inch ground clearance, improves the boxy EV’s breakover angle, making it better suited for rough roads.

The startup says it can build around 100 units per year, but exact details haven’t been ironed out yet. In an Out of Spec Review video, Geoffrey Hoffman, the company’s founder, said that he doesn’t have a precise plan for the short term, but that attending SEMA will help in identifying what people actually want.

Hoffman expects the pricing to be somewhere between the Slate Truck and the Tesla Cybertruck, so from $26,400 all the way up to $77,000, if the base dual-motor Cybertruck is the upper target.

The doors, the roof, and most of the seats are removable, and the vehicle is titled as an 11-seat bus. All of the structure and body parts are powder-coated aluminum, while the exposed fasteners are stainless steel or steel coated with 1,000-hour salt spray resistance. Inside, the fasteners are stainless or zinc-plated steel. All of the new materials are recycled, except for a few small 3D-printed parts.

If and when sales eventually kick off, the Badger will be available as a ready-made vehicle with whatever top hat the customer wants, or as a kit with a VIN. In the latter case, the customer will have to source a donor Tesla Model 3 or Model Y.

There’s no estimated range, but seeing how it’s shaped like a brick, it will most likely be less than the donor car’s original figure. That said, Hoffman said that its boxy EV may deliver more range around town compared to the Model 3 or Model Y, simply because the Badger is lighter. In the first quarter of 2027, the aerodynamics will be improved, according to the startup.

Hoffman’s main business is converting old British cars to electric. Its portfolio includes the DeLorean DMC-12, the classic Volkswagen Beetle, classic Land Rovers, and vintage Rolls-Royce and Bentley models.

#4525. Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production

Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.

The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.

Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:

The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.

This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August, when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.

Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.

For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.

The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.

Tesla also tried the opposite approach earlier this year. It offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 in February for “only the next 10 days,” then pulled it. A single-motor RWD version was discontinued after just 173 sales. None of it moved the needle.

The Cybertruck isn’t sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets, and Tesla canceled it for Australia and New Zealand last month.

So, Tesla has now discontinued more models than it currently offers. Looks like the great leader isn’t particularly good at writing product specs. And the hype has been over for quite a while anyway. In Europe, owning a Tesla has actually become something of an image liability.

This is what a wind-down looks like. Tesla isn’t trying to sell more Cybertrucks anymore. It’s trying to make as much money as possible on the last ones, with the hope that announcing the end of production will encourage some people to secure their order.

Once you’ve decided to end a program, volume stops mattering. You have a set number of build slots left, a parts supply you want to burn down, and probably a small group of fans who’ll want one before it’s gone. Pausing the cheapest trim and charging $7,500 more for the rest is the obvious play. You push everyone into higher-margin configurations and stop pretending the base truck is a real product.

But it does say a lot about the last two years of Cybertruck pricing. Tesla went from a $59,990 “limited-time” offer in February to a $92,490 entry price in November. That’s a company that never figured out who the truck was for.

#4524. VW And Skoda EV Owners Have Waited Years For Battery Preconditioning. It's Finally Coming

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The first Volkswagen ID.4 and Skoda Enyaq electric crossovers to roll off the assembly lines back in 2020 marked a big step for the two automakers, but owners quickly faced an uncomfortable truth: their high-voltage batteries could not be preconditioned for fast charging, which resulted in longer-than-expected charging times during cold weather.

That’s no longer the case, though, as both Skoda and Volkswagen are releasing a new over-the-air software update that adds the long-awaited feature to the oldest Enyaq, ID.4, and ID.5 EVs on the road, manufactured from 2020 to 2024. From 2024 onward, all three models came with an automatic battery preconditioning feature, so they don’t need improvements in this area.

In the Skoda Enyaq’s case, software version 3.9 adds the battery pre-heating function, as well as an updated welcome screen that no longer needs user confirmation to boot up completely. Various security updates and a software fix for the Online Connectivity Unit (OCU) are also included.

Roughly 200,000 Enyaq EVs are scheduled to get the update, with the rollout happening in waves. The first cars will receive the new feature starting in the second half of November, followed by another wave two weeks later.

Owners of cars that have version 3.8 will be prompted to install the latest version, which happens automatically over the air. If an older version is running in the vehicle, the car will need to install version 3.8 first, which prepares the car for the battery pre-heating function, while version 3.8 introduces the function itself.

Meanwhile, cars running version 2.x will need a visit to an authorized service center to get the latest software updates that enable battery pre-conditioning.

The same improvements are also being offered to the Volkswagen ID.4 and ID.5, though the software version that includes them is 3.9.1. The latest ID. Software iteration also improves the reliability of the electric door handles and AC charging.

It’s worth noting that the new battery preconditioning feature that’s coming to older Enyaq, ID.4, and ID.5 EVs can only be manually activated on a new virtual screen in the infotainment system. What’s more, the button that turns on battery heating is only active when the battery temperature is below 68°F (20°C), according to Jiří Vlček, Skoda project manager for online updates. The new software also shows the battery’s current temperature, so drivers can easily monitor it.

Skoda engineers tested the new feature in freezing conditions.

After pressing the preconditioning button, the battery starts to gradually heat up until it reaches its optimum temperature of roughly 77°F (25°C). This can take about 30 to 40 minutes, and the automakers recommend that drivers take this into account when driving to a fast charger.

If the battery is at an optimal temperature, it can accept a higher power from a DC fast charger, shortening the time it takes to get back on the road.

„From the user’s perspective, battery pre-heating is a very simple and straightforward function, but from our perspective it requires intervention in the three most important control units of the vehicle: the vehicle control unit, the battery control unit and the infotainment system,” said Vlček. “This places enormous demands on implementation and on comprehensive testing to ensure the update functions correctly.”

Before this update, some owners had to resort to do-it-yourself methods to manually activate battery preconditioning, which involved a custom-made microcontroller or a dedicated diagnostics dongle and an OBD programming app. Now, owners can enjoy faster charging in freezing conditions without having to jerry-rig a feature that, by the looks of it, has always been possible.

#4522. Kia’s PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9

Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.

The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.

A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.

Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.

It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.

The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

That’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.

Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.

It will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia said the new PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.

A plena capacidad la nueva #PV7 consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero #Kia #KiaPV7 #MovementThatInspires pic.twitter.com/fzIvviYZuE

Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.

Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.

Thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.

With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.

The PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.

Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.

The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.

Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.

The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.

The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.

Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.

The system runs Android Automotive OS, making it more like a smartphone with apps and customizable screens. It also includes Hyundai’s Gleo AI, an AI-powered in-car companion that can answer questions, control navigation or vehicle functions, and more.

Nice vehicle but once again Kia/Hyundai short changes on battery capacity. A 138" (3500 mm) wheelbase means plenty of room for a 140-150kwh battery (BMW and Rivian do that with vastly less space). That would give it a proper EPA range of over 300 miles with passengers or cargo. Instead this will be in the low 200s unloaded and 170-190 IRL. Offer it as a $7k upgrade. smh

Kia said the PV7 is based on a “Mobile Workspace” concept, with a layered dashboard and center console to optimize space.

The Kia PV7 Passenger and Cargo will go on sale in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. It will then roll out to new markets with new derivatives and conversions.

Kia will announce PV7 prices closer to its launch. In Korea, the PV5 Passenger and Cargo Compact starts at 45.9 million won ($34,000) and 41 million won ($30,000), respectively. In Germany, the PV5 Passenger 5-seater starts at €38,690 ($43,000).

#4521. The Lincoln Aviator PHEV May Have Died In America, But It’s Coming Back In China

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

While the Lincoln Aviator PHEV died in 2024 for most of the world, its nameplate will carry on in China. This week, China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) exposed homologation details of Lincoln’s all-new PHEV crossover, the Lincoln Aviator EX8. But while the old Aviator was a luxe version of the U.S.-designed Ford Explorer, this car is developed largely through a joint venture with one of China’s homegrown brands.

The Aviator EX8 is one of Ford China’s most recent attempts at competing in China’s fierce new energy vehicle (NEV) market. About a year ago, Ford released the Bronco New Energy, a Kia EV9-sized EREV and full EV crossover developed with and made by Ford’s joint venture partner, JMC. This Aviator feels similar in concept; however, it is made by Ford’s other joint venture partner, Changan. Changan Ford produces many Chinese-market versions of Ford combustion vehicles we are familiar with, like the Ford Escape. It also produces the U.S. market versions of the Lincoln Corsair and Nautilus.

Dimensionally, the Aviator EX8 is roughly the same size as the old Aviator, but its powertrain feels like it should be more competitive in China’s market. Instead of a V6 turbo engine, the car uses a Changan-made 1.5-liter turbocharged engine good for 148 horsepower. However, the MIIT filing has not revealed the Aviator’s electric motor setup or output, nor has it revealed the battery size and range the EX8 will have. It also has roof-mounted lidar, so I expect some level of advanced driver-assist features to be present when this car launches.

I find the Aviator EX8 to be handsome, even in the unflattering patent-style photos of China’s MIIT. It’s boxy, yet still adorned with a remarkable level of exterior finishing. The wheel choices suit the crossover’s style well; it looks big and expensive, just like a Lincoln should. In all, it looks like a shrunken version of the Lincoln Navigator. If it has a similar interior to what we’ve seen from Lincoln’s other models, then the Aviator EX8 could be a compelling PHEV entry.

And it needs to be compelling, because Lincoln’s Chinese presence is very limited, while competition is hot. For starters, Lincoln has no NEV in China. It used to sell the Corsair PHEV, but it was discontinued when the model was facelifted for 2026. If Lincoln wants to continue to sell cars in China, it needs products that are better marketed to Chinese buyers. In China, this car will face a large number of midsize PHEV or EREV competitors, some of which we’ve got our hands on, like the Lynk & Co 08.

There’s very little chance the Aviator EX8 will exit China and enter our market. Even though Lincoln is importing cars to the U.S., it plans to discontinue the China-made Nautilus and Corsair by 2030 and make more vehicles here. Also, given its development with Changan, it likely would not be compliant with the U.S. connected cars ban.

#4520. GM Could Make Variable-Compression Engines Easier to Service

A newly published patent application details how to apply the efficiency tech to longitudinal engines.

GM engineers spend a lot of time thinking about engines, and the company’s patent-to-production pipeline is hard evidence. Cylinder deactivation and sliding camshafts? GM has brought its own versions of both to production. Making truck V-8s bigger and more powerful without completely sacrificing efficiency? Coming right up. Their next target may be applying existing fuel-saving tech to a wider array of engines.

A few engineers in particular have been tinkering with ways to adopt a variable-compression ratio, and specifically how the necessary hardware can be packaged with a longitudinal engine. Related patents go back about a decade. (Nissan already sells a variable-compression engine of its own, the somewhat disappointing VC-Turbo, but that one is designed for transverse front- and all-wheel-drive applications.)

See all results for used cars for sale near 48085

In a previous patent filing, GM outlined how it would locate the control shaft, necessary for varying compression in its design, up above the crankshaft. The compression variability—approximately 7:1 to 11:1—comes by way of a special connecting-rod linkage. The connecting rod attaches to one end of a center link that’s mounted on the crankshaft, and the other end of the center link connects through a control rod to the control shaft. The design also includes a phaser that adjusts the control shaft’s rotational timing relative to the crankshaft, thus controlling the piston’s movement and varying the compression.

And one bonus compared with Nissan's system, which uses valve timing to achieve the Atkinson-cycle effect, GM’s arrangement would allow for the expansion stroke to be longer than the compression stroke—up to 40 percent longer—which has potential efficiency benefits. Note that Honda has commercialized a similar extended-expansion engine concept, which it calls EXlink, that’s used in household cogeneration units that supply both electricity and hot water.

Now comes an innovation that could push a variable-compression longitudinal engine closer to reality. A recently published U.S. patent application shows how GM could make this happen. In a nutshell, it would replace the center link with a two-piece assembly assembled around the crankshaft. One part would connect to the piston rod, and the other to the control rod.

See all results for used cars for sale near 48085

The description also says the bolts used to make up the connection would be accessible from below the engine, likely with the oil pan removed. GM also explains that placing the control shaft above the crankshaft makes room for the engine’s mounts or the vehicle’s steering or four-wheel-drive equipment that normally sit below a longitudinally oriented engine.

GM says this design would allow conventional lubrication of the connecting rods. Together with the two-piece center link, that could mean the GM design is both easier to service and less prone to bearing-related problems.

The patent drawings show a gas inline-six, a gasoline engine layout GM doesn’t currently use, but that’s not evidence that such a configuration is in the offing. The same concept could be applied to something like the L3B 2.7-liter four-cylinder—the one with sliding cam sleeves—that’s used in Chevy and GMC half-ton trucks and could find its way into a new Camaro or Buick sedan.

#4519. The BMW iX3 smashed its EPA range rating, driving well over 400 miles in a real-world test

BMW’s new iX3 outperformed the Volvo EX60 and Mercedes-Benz GLC EV, driving well over 400 miles during a real-world range test.

In a recent nationally representative survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

The study found that 73% consider 75 miles of range, or less, enough to cover their daily driving. Meanwhile, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range to consider an EV.

Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in 10 minutes.

BMW’s new iX3 checks all the boxes. Based on BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive 800V system, the 2027 iX3 50 xDrive delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles (with 20″ summer tires).

With the 22″ summer tires, the iX3 50 xDrive has an EPA-estimated range of up to 392 miles. Still, plenty for at least a week of commuting.

It can also add 170-185 miles of range in 10 minutes with up to 400 kW DC fast charging. In everyday, real-world driving, it may drive even further than its official EPA numbers suggest.

During Edmunds‘ EV Range test, the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive (with 22″ summer tires) drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles.

The electric SUV was also more efficient than advertised. The iX3 achieved an energy consumption of 28.3 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles by roughly 11.6%.

BMW’s new iX3 is now the longest-range luxury electric SUV that Edmunds has tested, outperforming rivals including the 2027 Volvo EX60 (352 miles) and Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric (392 miles).

The Edmunds real-world range test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions.

It consists of 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

The 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive is available to order in Sport, M Sport, and M Sport Professional trims, priced from $61,500, $64,000, and $65,500, respectively.

Average speed of 40 mph in perfect weather is an absolute best case scenario for EVs. I think cold weather 70 mph would be the worst case and it should be tested.

That said, I think BMW and Mercedes tend to underrate their cars published range (I think they publish worst case condition range). BMW iX and Mercedes have historically outperformed EPA ratings according to various articles and reddits posts.

But I think regardless of what we think of Edmunds tests, these are some crazy range figures and with roughly 100kwh usable battery capacity, you are still looking at close to 4 miles per kwh. As an example across the Ultium platform anything from Chevy or Cadillac barely breaches 300 miles. The big Escalade and pickup trucks have 225+ kwh battery so I am not counting them.

If the depreciation rate for luxury EVs holds up, in 2-3 years, they will be awesome value.

#4518. This Chinese EV Maker Wants To Put A Foot Bath In The Back Seat Of Your Car. Really

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

If you've ever been in the back of a Rolls-Royce, you'll know just how lovely its rear lambswool carpets are. Their shag is so deep, soft, and luxurious that it's a crime to keep your shoes on back there. While enjoying them, you might think they're the pinnacle of rear seat foot comfort. However, Chinese EV maker Deepal wants to one-up even Rolls-Royce, with an extendable backseat foot bath.

According to Australia's Which Car?, Changan sub-brand Deepal recently filed a patent for a foot bath that would extend out from under the front seats, so that passengers can literally wash their feet while on the move. Once extended, rear passengers can place their feet in the water, which is presumably heated, and even massage them on rollers at the bottom of the basin. Hopefully, there's a towel rack or cubby back there, otherwise you're taking wet feet out and soaking the carpets, which sounds like a nightmare for interior mold.

What about sloshing? I can't even drive around with a Wawa coffee cup filled near the top or it'll slosh out of the spout onto my center console. So how is a basin of water not going to toss all of its water onto the floor at the first bump or turn? According to Car Expert, Deepal's patent claims that the basin can actually block the water from sloshing out. It also has guide holes which let sloshing water recirculate into the bottom, keeping the liquid level low.

There's also a disinfection assembly, to keep the water from being gross, and a quick disconnect to dispose of the water from the vehicle body.

Will this technology ever actually make production? Who knows, as automakers often patent wild ideas just to future-proof their ability to make it one day. But foot baths are quite popular in China, so who knows, maybe there's enough demand for this sort of thing. If it never makes production (which seems likely),though, I think some deep carpets and no shoes, Die Hard-style, will do just fine.

#4515. BioWare Documentary Slated for Release in 2027

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

It’s been a few weeks now since the sudden announcement of EA’s closure of BioWare, longtime developer of the fan-favorite Mass Effect series. The major fervor surrounding this landmark closure, as well as the cancellation of the next Mass Effect, has gradually started to die down, and all that’s left is a sad little hole in our hearts where hope for a new spacefaring adventure once lived.

In spite of its unfortunate denouement, it doesn’t change the fact that BioWare was, is, and shall always remain a beloved studio, whose stories and worlds touched many a heart. In fact, BioWare and its staff were something of hometown heroes to its origin in the city of Edmonton, Canada. Because of this, a production effort has been spurred forth by the Canadian entertainment industry to properly document the studio’s 30-plus years of history.

For an in-depth look at how we lost one of the gaming greats, this is how the fall of BioWare was years in the making.

According to a Deadline exclusive published today, a documentary outlining the history of BioWare, from its founding in 1995 to its closure this year, is in production now, with hopes to have it up on screens sometime next year, including a run through all of the major film festivals. This will be the definitive BioWare story, told not just by its staff, but the many fans whose lives were changed by its productions.

The documentary, titled “Massive Effect: The BioWare Story,” is being written by Canadian writer and director Akash Sherman, best known for his 2018 sci-fi film, Clara. Interestingly, the actual filming process for this documentary began about two years ago, which means everything was already well underway the moment the decision came down from EA to shutter the studio. Sherman and his crew have captured the moment the BioWare story came to an end, as well as the rippling effects it had on the gaming community.

The actual filming process for this documentary began about two years ago.

The headliners of the documentary are BioWare’s three original founders, Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, though it’s also slated to feature appearances by a variety of other game industry alumni, including Lucasfilm Games Vice President Douglas Reilly, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic director Casey Hudson, Game Awards creator Geoff Keighley, and even EA’s infamous former CEO, John Riccitiello.

A ranking list of all the games BioWare has ever developed in the history of the studio.

“When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved,” Muzyka and Zeschuk said in a statement obtained by Deadline. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward.”

The film’s creation and production is something of a love letter from BioWare’s home turf of Canada. In fact, its creation was commissioned by Canada’s Super Channel, with the Canada Media Fund offering support throughout the production.

“We are thrilled to bring Massive Effect: The BioWare Story to Canadian audiences,” Kim Ball, EVP of Content & Communications for Super Channel told Deadline. “As an Edmonton-based company, we’re especially proud to celebrate BioWare’s extraordinary hometown story and the people, creativity and groundbreaking storytelling behind some of the most beloved games of a generation.”

The film’s producers are inviting BioWare’s fans to contribute photos, videos, and stories of how BioWare’s games have affected their lives, with a select few slated to be featured in the film. “BioWare’s fans have been part of its journey since the very first game,” said one of the film’s producers, Adam Scorgie. “It’s only right that they help us tell the rest of the story.”

Sherman himself has similar reverence for BioWare, saying that their games are what helped ignite his initial creative spark, and that it was his “privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling.”

There's still a chance that Mass Effect can survive.

#4514. Tesla's Kickflipping Roadster Looks Like A Great Way To Lose Your Lunch

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Car companies have spent the last 140 years figuring out how to perfect ground travel. Tesla decided that winning that war was unimaginative at best. And as we've all seen by now, the carmaker instead took its next-gen Roadster to the sky last month to demonstrate what it might look like to own a flying car one day.

But what would it actually be like to drive (fly?) the thing? This week, Tesla released a video showing a first-person camera view of the Roadster executing its rad kick-flip maneuver and other stunts. It does not look pleasant to experience firsthand.

If you watched the Roadster unveiling last month, this all probably looks familiar. It's the same stunts we saw that day, including the upside-down dive off of the half-pipe and the jump-spin over the Tesla Semi. But seeing it from the car's perspective adds a whole new layer to it, and shows this dizzying experience a person would have from the cockpit.

Watching the cold gas thrusters at work up close during the kickflip gives you a sense of how much goes into ensuring that the car stays upright. The car adjusts the volume of nitrogen that it releases in order to prevent car from over-rotating and transferring from a barrel roll to an out-of-control corkscrew. Just one simple nudge and it lands back on all four wheels.

Then there's the nosedive off of the half-pipe. A bit more correcting to keep the roll and yaw in check—but the Roadster does it without a hiccup.

All of these amazing stunts happened without a driver; Tesla put a dummy in the front seat. Many actual human beings might feel dizzy or even sick from these kinds of tricks.

Tesla hasn't published what kind of g-forces the kickflip generates, but watching the onboard footage also makes me wonder what kind of fighter pilot-style harness and big bolsters are needed to keep the driver in-place versus the road-going version of the car. Heck, you might need to be a fighter pilot to endure these maneuvers.

It's really hard not to appreciate how much engineering went into making the demo happen. Sure, it takes hours to fill up the 600-liter ultra-high-pressure composite-overwrapped pressure vessels with 10,000 PSI of nitrogen for just a few seconds of joy. But man, is it cool to watch from just about any perspective.

And while Tesla can't guarantee that the flying version of its car will reach a single driveway (or be road legal, for that matter), it's still a very cool, very over-engineered party trick unlike anything we'll likely see from a car manufacturer again. If you're going to buy one and put it through its paces, though, I'd recommend having a light lunch.

#4511. Tesla Is Now Powering One Of Its Biggest Charging Rivals

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Superchargers aren't just a Tesla thing anymore. Today EVgo announced that it opened its first location powered by Tesla hardware. The 12-stall charging station in Chicago kicks off an expansion that will include hundreds more Supercharger stalls nationwide, EVgo said.

With the shift to the North American Charging Standard (NACS), Tesla has shifted in some aspects toward a brand-agnostic tech provider. The NACS port was once a Tesla exclusive; now it’s the port of choice when it comes to modern EVs. Similarly, Tesla’s V4 Supercharging cabinets are available for purchase and installation by any commercial client. Tesla's V4 Supercharging cabinets are powerful, offering speeds up to 500 kW.

“Deploying our first EVgo Supercharger marks an important milestone in growing our customer base while supporting the EV industry’s transition to NACS,” said EVgo CEO Badar Khan.

The first EVgo location in Chicago has both CCS and NACS ports, thanks to the Magic Dock connector. The first batch of Tesla-powered EVgo stations will be built at grocery stores and shopping outlet centers owned by real estate company Regency Centers. This developer has had a longstanding partnership with EVgo; it already had plans to implement 400 more charging stalls. It says that Illinois is a great place to start its Supercharger push, since EV registrations have grown 60% over the past two years.

One nice bonus for Tesla drivers: EVgo’s Superchargers come up in Tesla’s in-car navigation system. As long as the “third-party charging” box is checked in the Tesla navigation app, users will be able to navigate to and charge just as easily as they would for a normal Tesla Supercharging station.

EVgo’s expansion spans more than just one developer or a handful of NACS ports. The company says it already is on track to hit 500 NACS-enabled charging stations nationwide (not counting the Supercharging network). Within the next two years, it wants all of its existing stations built after 2023 to have at least one NACS plug.

Tesla isn’t the only DC fast-charging company with hardware capable of charging natively via a NACS port. Once the NACS plug shape was officially certified by SAE, charging cabinet manufacturers quickly integrated it into their designs. However, Tesla’s Supercharging cabinets are known for their reliability. Tesla itself claims that uptime is 99%, and the network is known for being one of the best in the business.

#4508. BMW Is Giving New EV Buyers $500 In Free Charging

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW's latest Neue Klasse EVs push the boundaries of range and charging speed. In short, they're some damn good electric cars. Now there's another reason to buy one: free charging.

BMW on Thursday said it's offering $500 in public charging credits for 2027 electric models. It applies to the i5, i7, and iX3, and is open to drivers who buy or lease. The benefits last for one year from the car's purchase date.

Here's how the $500 breaks down. BMW says $300 of it can be redeemed at more than 15 charging networks, including Ionna, Shell Recharge, ChargePoint, and EVgo. The other $200 only applies to Ionna locations. (BMW is one of the automakers backing Ionna.)

To access the funds, drivers need to set up an account through the BMW app. Once they do that and handle payment through BMW ChargingNetwork, credits are automatically applied to eligible charging purchases.

BMW is also offering buyers of 2027 EVs one free year of Ionna membership, which gets drivers 25% discounts on sessions at the fast-growing charging player.

If $500 in free charging sounds nice and you're considering these vehicles, I have one note of caution after getting behind the wheel of all three.

The i5 is a solid all-around EV. It drives well, looks familiar, and offers over 300 miles of range in some trims. But the i7 and iX3 are miles ahead in terms of onboard technology and specs. The latter models use BMW's Neue Klasse architecture and feature an overhauled digital interface with a wonderful "Panoramic Vision" display below the windshield. The iX3 offers over 400 miles of range and 400 kilowatt charging. Expect similar capabilities to trickle throughout BMW's lineup and into the next iteration of the i5 too.

#4507. BYD is launching this 5-seat luxury electric SUV next week with over 1,000 km of range

BYD’s luxury brand, Denza, calls it “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles.” The new Denza N8 electric SUV will launch next week, offering an impressive CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles), massive digital screens, and plenty of premium extras.

After opening pre-orders for the new 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, said the results so far “have been excellent.”

According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.

That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

While Li confirmed last week that the new EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.

Now, it’s official. Denza announced on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.

BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.

The Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

It’s available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).

The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will use either a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) and 800 km (497 miles), respectively.

The Denza N8 also features BYD’s latest Flash Charging technology, letting it recharge from 10% to 80% in just five minutes. It takes just nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

Like most of its new luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.

Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.

The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.

BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

#4506. Gas Prices Got You Down? This 261-MPG Volkswagen Solves That—For $140,000

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

In 2013, VW launched one of the most fascinating experiments in fuel efficiency ever made. The Volkswagen XL1 took 12 years to develop and ended up costing a whopping $150,000 at the time. However, as an engineering exercise, it was brilliant. And since VW only made 250, it's even rarer than a Bugatti Veyron from the same era.

If you're looking for an extreme answer to high gas prices, today's your lucky day. There's currently an XL1 in the Netherlands up for auction on Catawiki. The 2016 model up for grabs has just over 1,000 miles on the odometer and is apparently in excellent condition inside and out.

The XL1 project was spearheaded by Ferdinand Piech, VW's top boss at the time. Not known to ever give up on his lofty, ambitious goals, Piech fought for 12 years, and through several iterations, to finally achieve his "one liter" car, something that could burn just one liter of fuel per every 100 km. VW pulled out all the stops to make it extraordinarily efficient; the result was something closer to a supercar than a Toyota Prius.

That teardrop-shaped body is made from carbon fiber, as is its chassis, saving weight. It debuted a full year before BMW's i3, an EV/PHEV which only had a carbon chassis but a plastic body. The car has butterfly doors and two seats that are offset to optimize the car's aerodynamic shape.

Power comes from an 800cc, two-cylinder, turbo-diesel engine behind the driver—this makes it mid-engine, like a supercar—plus a plug-in hybrid system centered around a 5.5 kilowatt-hour battery. The plug-in hybrid powertrain wasn't originally planned, and didn't come about until near the end of its development, so it needed a massive 50-pound removable charging box in the trunk so you could plug it in.

With a funky hybrid powertrain, a curb weight of just 1,852 pounds, and a drag coefficient of just 0.189, the XL1 was capable of an EU-tested 0.9 liters per 100 km, which equates to 261 mpg. It can also travel 31 miles on battery power alone, registering an insane efficiency of 6.2 miles per kWh, about double today's more conventional EVs. VW said at the time of the XL1's launch that it only needed about 8 horsepower to sustain a steady 62 mph.

The main downside is performance: It only makes 68 horsepower, so it takes almost 13 seconds to get to 60 mph.

This specific car up for auction is expected to fetch around $140,000, according to the auction house. So even with its incredible fuel economy and currently outrageous fuel prices, the XL1's financial breakeven point is still a long ways away. Plus, it runs on diesel, which has seen even steeper price spikes than regular gas. A used EV cuts you off from the gas station entirely, and is a better all-around choice of course.

But for someone who wants an amazing piece of automotive history, the XL1 could be worth the price. Plus, it'll sip on fuel like no other for many of your daily errands—and look cool doing it.

#4505. EVgo opens its first Tesla Superchargers, with hundreds more planned

EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo plans to add across the US.

The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.

The Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.

“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” said Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.

EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

Smart move on EVGo's part. More reliable charger at a lower cost than they can build themselves, and Tesla takes on all the maintenance and network operations for a slice of the sales.

EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The company aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it plans to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

#4504. Everything Announced at GOG’s First-Ever Showcase Event

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

I know that I'm not the only one who has always appreciated GOG as a sacred sanctuary for classic PC titles, but its latest event proves the platform is doing much more than just keeping old games running.

That's because, to celebrate its 18th anniversary, the team held its first-ever showcase, and it was packed with updates that have me genuinely excited about where the platform is heading – and you should be too!

Broadcast today, Thursday, November 5, on YouTube, the first-ever GOG Showcase caught everyone's attention with a variety of announcements, ranging from new games and features to an entirely new publishing initiative.

For starters, co-founder Miho Kinski perfectly summed up the platform's philosophy at the beginning of the event, making it clear that its mission remains unchanged: "We wanted games to live forever. Not for a season, not until the servers shut down, but for as long as people want them to play." And honestly, that message really resonated throughout the presentation.

Then, the event kicked off by celebrating the GOG Patrons program, and the numbers are pretty impressive: more than 10,000 supporters have helped preserve over 300 games, ensuring they run flawlessly on modern systems with the help of more than 1,700 technical fixes.

Bit Kid shadowdrops Knytt Classic for free on Steam and GOG.

And speaking of games, the showcase also had plenty of nostalgia in store, with the announcement of Wing Commander Anniversary Editions. The series is returning in grand fashion with its 35th and 30th Anniversary collections, featuring both legacy and updated versions of the games. Oh, and if you already own these titles, the new editions will automatically appear in your library!

The expansion of GOG's classic game collection doesn't stop there, either. The original Road Rash has also officially joined the platform today, giving fans another opportunity to revisit this beloved classic.

The event kicked off by celebrating the GOG Patrons program, and the numbers are pretty impressive: more than 10,000 supporters have helped preserve over 300 games, ensuring they run flawlessly on modern systems with the help of more than 1,700 technical fixes.

However, perhaps the biggest surprise was the reveal of Retrovibe by GOG, a new publishing initiative focused on bringing previously unreleased games with a "classic soul" to modern audiences. This marks the company's first major step into publishing, and it's an interesting evolution for a store that has spent nearly two decades acting as a digital harbor for gaming history.

Fans can look forward to bringing lost games back from the dead.

And when it comes to new features, that wasn't all the showcase had to offer. GOG also introduced GOG Social, a new social network integrated into the platform that allows users to share screenshots, videos, and participate in discussions, all directly connected to the games they own.

Finally, the team confirmed what many of us have been asking for: a completely rebuilt GOG GALAXY. The launcher has been redesigned for Windows and Mac, promising better performance and, most importantly, full Linux support. Yeah... I used to pray for times like this!

Eighteen years of keeping games alive is no small feat, and based on these announcements, the next chapter for GOG looks just as bright. As the team emphasized during its first-ever showcase, "18 years of making games live forever together." I've always relied on the platform to revisit some of my favorite childhood titles, but with these new social features and its expansion into publishing, I have a feeling I'll be spending a lot more time exploring its library in the years to come!

#4502. Tesla Is Killing The Cybertruck To Make Room For More Robotaxis

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The controversial Tesla Cybertruck electric pickup will be retired next year, CEO Elon Musk confirmed on X. The angular truck went on sale at the end of 2023 and instantly became a social statement—for better or worse.

Production of the Cybertruck will start winding down next summer at the company’s Texas Gigafactory, and the extra floor space will be used to build more Cybercabs.

The unpainted truck had a short burst in popularity at the beginning of its production run, but interest fizzled, and sales never reached the potential that Musk and Tesla had envisioned back in 2019, when the vehicle was first presented as a concept.

In this year’s third quarter, the Cybertruck amassed 4,323 sales, according to data from Cox Automotive. From January through September, sales totaled 11,586 units. Tesla doesn’t break out individual sales figures for the Cybertruck, but industry estimates put the vehicle’s overall deliveries at roughly 70,000.

That’s a far cry from the hundreds of thousands of sales recorded every quarter by the Model 3 and Model Y. It’s also another reminder that electric pickups haven’t quite taken off as their manufacturers had hoped, and Tesla is now taking the fall, just like Ford did with the F-150 Lightning, which went the way of the dodo last year after lackluster sales and ballooning costs.

There’s no denying that you either love or hate the Cybertruck, just like there’s no denying that Tesla dared to do things like no other car manufacturer before it. Sure, some might argue that the angular EV looks like an unpolished fridge, but it brought steer-by-wire and a 48-volt low-voltage architecture to the masses. Whether or not they’ll be adopted by other companies is another story, though.

At roughly the same time as Elon Musk’s announcement that Cybertruck production would wind down in the middle of 2027, Tesla stopped taking orders for the entry-level Dual-Motor All-Wheel Drive version of the model, leaving just the Premium and Cyberbeast trims available to order on the automaker’s website.

Additionally, the price of the remaining models has been increased. The Premium AWD model now starts at $92,490, up from $89,990, while the top Cyberbeast now costs $102,490, up from $99,990. The most recent price bumps come after a similar move in August.
