#4501. Hyundai’s $359 IONIQ 5 lease looks like a deal, but don’t overlook its bigger sibling

The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in America outside of Tesla, but its larger three-row sibling looks like the better deal right now.

Through September, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 was the third top-selling EV in the US, behind the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.

Hyundai’s electric SUV is outselling rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, and Toyota bZ.

Why? For one, it’s one of the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at about $35,000, and Hyundai has been offering some of the most attractive lease deals.

After the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September last year, Hyundai responded by reducing prices on the IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims.

The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250. That’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model adds $2,500, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, starts at $58,955, or nearly $24,000 more than the base IONIQ 5 SE.

On Hyundai’s website, the 2027 IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range is available to lease from $359 a month. The offer is for a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing for an effective cost of $567 per month.

The extended-range Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE RWD can be leased from $369 a month. The offer is also a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing, for an effective cost of $577 per month.

Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9, meanwhile, is available to lease from $419 a month. That deal also includes $4,999 due at signing, but is for a 36-month lease, so the effective cost is $557 per month.

Using Hyundai’s payment calculator, it would cost about $412 a month to lease the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE for 36 months with $4,999 due at signing. With an effective cost of $550 per month, it’s only $7 less than the three-row IONIQ 9.

The Hyundai IONIQ 9 offers more range than its smaller sibling, with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles for the base SE trim.

The IONIQ 5 is a midsize electric SUV, about the same size as a Tesla Model Y, with two rows and enough room for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating and six- or seven-seat configurations.

With an added row of seating, the IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with the IONIQ 5, which offers up to 106.5 cubic feet.

While the IONIQ 9 may be the better deal right now, the IONIQ 5 is still a good fit for those looking for a smaller, more efficient SUV that doesn’t necessarily need the added space.

In comparison, the standard Tesla Model Y RWD is listed for lease starting at $499 a month with an EPA range of up to 321 miles. That’s for a 36-month lease with $3,000 down.

Using Tesla’s payment calculator, if you put the same $4,999 down for a 24-month lease like the IONIQ 5, the Model Y RWD’s monthly rate is $549.

Which one would you choose? The IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, or Tesla Model Y? Let us know why in the comments.

Both the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are built at Hyundai’s Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

I really haven’t seen much value in leasing. I’d rather buy the car outright using cash, with the goal of keeping the car for 10+ years.

My family recently bought a Hyundai IONIQ 5, and it is an outstanding car. Loaded with great features — both on the EV side and then for safety and comfort.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told us that its electric SUVs are attracting new buyers to the brand at a higher rate than its gas or hybrid vehicles.

The IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

#4500. Over A Quarter Of BMW, Mini, And Rolls-Royce Models Sold In Q3 Had A Plug

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The BMW Group, which operates the BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce car brands, saw 20% of its global vehicle sales in the third quarter represented by all-electric models. Adding plug-in hybrids increases the electrified models’ share to 27.4%, the company said in its latest earnings report.

From the beginning of the year through September, EVs have accounted for 18.4% of the three automakers’ total sales worldwide, with PHEVs raising the figure to 26.1%.

Despite the promising numbers, the automotive group clearly has a regionalization problem on its hands. Europe is leading the way by a wide margin, with 34.7% of sales represented by EVs and 46.9% by all electrified models.

Meanwhile, over in the United States, just 4.7% of BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce models sold were EVs. That’s a huge difference, and it puts the U.S. at the bottom of the BMW Group’s list for electrification. By comparison, Chinese EV sales amounted to 6.5%, while the Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa regions totaled 18% EV sales.

The only thing that saves the day for the company’s electrified lineup in the U.S. is plug-in hybrids, which, together with EVs, had an 11.4% share in the third quarter. It’s also worth noting that the new iX3 and i3 models are just starting to trickle down to American dealers, and the U.S. also doesn’t get the electric iX2 and iX2 that Europeans have access to. The updated i7 is also on its way, but that has always been a low-volume car that never made a meaningful impact on the company’s sales reports.

What’s more, even though one in every five BMW Group models was all-electric in Q3, the company’s year-to-date numbers aren’t so promising. Globally, the group sold 314,552 EVs and 131,653 PHEVs from January through September, a 5.1% decrease compared to the same period last year. EVs saw a 2.7% drop, while PHEV sales declined 10.3%.

The only positive number in the company’s electrification Excel sheets has to do with how many EVs were sold in comparison to everything else in the portfolio. In the first three quarters of 2026, the share of EV sales within the BMW Group reached 18.4%, up from last year’s 18%.

Things should improve once the iX3 and i3 are widely available everywhere in the world, but they’re not guaranteed to be a success in the U.S., where policy whiplash has severely slowed the adoption of all-electric vehicles.

#4499. Apollo’s newest electric scooter is also its lowest-cost yet

Apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the company is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.

The new Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the company’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo says the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.

The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.

Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.

At 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an important compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.

Despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.

Apollo says it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance issues. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.

Perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The company says 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.

At $599, the Dash appears designed to get those riders into Apollo’s ecosystem much earlier – while also putting the company squarely into competition with the mass-market scooters it previously sat above.

And for those wanting a bit more power or features, Apollo’s more upmarket models are on sale now as part of early Black Friday promotions.

#4498. Amazon set to deploy more than 3,000 TATA electric delivery trucks

Amazon isn’t just electrifying its American delivery operations. The virtual big box stores that Bezos built understands the benefits of EVs as well as anyone, and they’re working hard to deploy electric vehicles everywhere they can. And now, that global push is extending to India.

Indian automaker TATA Motors has announced a deal with Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India. When it goes live, it will be the largest electric truck deployment by in India and mark Amazon’s most significant move to extend its Indian fleet electrification beyond last-mile logistics.

“India is accelerating towards electric mobility and the realization of Viksit Bharat 2047,” says Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy, Hon’ble Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Government of India. “The collaboration between TATA Motors and Amazon shows what that looks like in practice: sustained demand from a nationwide logistics network met by electric trucks manufactured in India. Through PM E-DRIVE, the Government will continue to support this transition, and I look forward to more such efforts in powering green logistics.”

In addition to being a big deal for TATA, the 3,000 electric truck deal represents a serous bump to India’s deployed electric truck fleet, and are a major step towards the wide-scale electrification of freight transportation across the country – that’s not just good for Amazon’s fuel bills, it’s good for everyone and everything that breathes air, too.

“Electrifying our logistics and transportation network is an important part of Amazon’s goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040,” says Abhinav Singh, Vice President, Operations, Amazon, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkey. “We have made significant progress in India, with more than 15,000 electric vehicles operating across 500-plus cities. To enable this transition, we are also supporting the development of infrastructure and solutions that make EV adoption easier for our carrier partners and drivers. We are now setting a bold vision to scale electric trucking, addressing one of the toughest challenges in decarbonizing transportation. Our collaboration with TATA Motors marks an important step towards realizing this vision. By combining our strengths, we aim to accelerate the deployment of electric trucks across more routes, starting with intracity operations and expanding to India’s major freight corridors.”

The truck Amazon will be deploying in these record numbers is a version of the Tata Ultra E.7, a 7.5-tonne (~16,000 lb.) straight truck powered by a 240 kW (~320 hp) electric motor drawing power from a 96 kWh LFP battery pack. The truck’s makers claim a loaded range of up to 130 km (~80 miles) on a single charge, with DC fast-charging that’s capable enough to keep the trucks charged up between deliveries.

Amazon’s new TATA electric delivery trucks will support the transport of goods between warehouse facilities – which means traveling across cities and along India’s national freight corridors.

#4497. China's World-Beating Supercar Just Hit 312 MPH

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

A Chinese EV is officially the fastest production car in the world and the first production car in history to break the 500 kilometers per hour (310 miles per hour) barrier. BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme, a two-door electric hypercar, reached 503.17 kph (312.6 mph) on a public road in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on November 1.

As a reminder, the U9 Xtreme was already the world’s fastest car, after it reached 496.22 kph (308.3 mph) back in September 2025, but the Chinese automaker had already set its sights last year on breaking the 500 kph barrier—something that no other production car has ever managed.

The latest and most impressive record happened on a roughly 10-kilometer (6.2-mile) stretch of the E11 road in Abu Dhabi’s Al Dhafra Region, which was closed to public traffic. German racing driver Marc Basseng, the same driver who delivered the previous record, was behind the wheel and needed four runs over the course of two days to set the new record.

The first two runs happened on October 31, when the maximum speed was 490 kph (304.4 mph). Engineers made adjustments to the vehicle’s aerodynamics, suspension settings, and tire pressures to improve stability and performance. Then, on the last run of the second day, the Racelogic recorder made the 503.17 kph (312.6 mph) run official.

According to Guinness World Records, the Yangwang U9 Xtreme now holds the records for the highest speed achieved by a production car and an electric production car in a single-direction run. The FIA also confirmed the achievement on its website.

That last part is particularly interesting because the usual way of breaking records involves two separate runs in opposite directions to account for elevation change, wind speed, and any potential breakdown. BYD went for a single run in a single direction, which could make companies like Rimac, Bugatti, and Koenigsegg raise an eyebrow and challenge BYD’s result.

Nevertheless, going over 500 kph in a production car—albeit a limited-production model—is immensely impressive, especially considering that it’s an EV. BYD plans to make just 30 units of the U9 Xtreme, which is the most powerful and fastest version of the U9 supercar. Powered by four electric motors totaling 2,977 horsepower, the Xtreme uses a 1,200-volt lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack that can discharge at a 30C rate. A set of semi-slick GitiSport e-GTR2 Pro tires keeps the car on the road and provides stopping power, helped by titanium calipers and carbon-ceramic rotors.

#4496. Honda just showed off its first high-end electric mountain bike

Honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes. Now the Japanese giant is adding another electrified vehicle to the list – a premium electric mountain bike.

Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market. And unlike many automotive-branded e-bikes that amount to little more than a licensing deal and a familiar logo slapped on someone else’s frame, Honda appears to have actually put some engineering muscle behind this one.

The RN0 was jointly developed with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.

There’s actually some real history behind that connection. Honda experimented with mountain bike development in the early 2000s, culminating in its wild RN01 downhill racing bike. In 2005, that project won the overall series championship in the UCI Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup. Honda never turned the RN01 into a consumer bicycle, but more than two decades later, the RN0 is effectively picking up where the company previously left off.

The roughly 24 kg (53 lb) RN0 is set up as a multi-role electric mountain bike, featuring 160 mm FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima front suspension paired with a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima rear shock. DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE wheels use a mullet setup with a 29-inch wheel up front and 27.5-inch wheel in the rear, while Shimano DEORE XT four-piston brakes handle stopping duties.

Those are some quality components, but the drivetrain may be even more interesting.

Honda is using Shimano’s new 2.3 kg drive unit, rated for up to 100 Nm of torque and 750 watts of maximum output, paired with a sizeable 720 Wh battery.

Shimano’s AUTO ASSIST can automatically vary motor assistance based on terrain and rider input, while AUTO SHIFT handles gear changes to maintain an appropriate cadence.

There’s even an Assist Carryover function that briefly continues providing power after pedaling stops, potentially making it easier to clear rocks, roots, and other technical obstacles that normally would see the assist grind to a halt right when it is needed most.

A 2.2-inch color display is integrated directly into the top tube, and there’s USB-C charging plus Shimano app connectivity for adjusting motor settings and electronically locking the bike.

Honda hasn’t yet announced pricing in its release, but with a carbon chassis, Factory-level FOX suspension, XT brakes, and premium Shimano electronics, don’t expect this to be the everyman’s electric bike.

If anything, the RN0 looks much more like Honda is finally bringing its motorcycle engineering mentality back to mountain bikes – this time with a battery and motor along for the ride.

#4495. 5 American, 6 Canadian: Workhorse W56 arrives in the True North

Electric truck brand Workhorse is bringing its W56 Class 5 and 6 electric trucks to Canada thanks to a new agreement with a Canadian dealer group and fleet management provider offering truck and trailer sales, parts, repair, and 24/7 roadside assistance and towing services across the Northern nation.

Building on years of electric step van deployments in Canada and underscoring the company’s commitment to Canada as a growth region, the new dealer agreement with Tristan Fleet Management marks the first-ever Canadian dealer partnership for Workhorse.

“Canadian fleets need proven electric trucks that deliver on quality and performance in any condition,” said James Griffin, Chief Revenue Officer at Workhorse. “The W56 has already proven itself on this front in real-world fleet service across Canada. Tristan’s strong reputation, its extensive network, and ability to provide around-the-clock roadside support will be extremely valuable as Workhorse continues to grow our presence in the country.”

Workhorse has been selling and supporting electric trucks in Canada since 2021 through its partnership with Purolator, a Canadian-owned leading integrated freight, package and logistics solutions provider that has grown alongside the rapid expansion of online shopping for everything from groceries to car parts and road-ready motorcycles has also seen the expansion of last-mile delivery contractors. These fleet operators and drivers are essential workers who keep the online economy rolling, and they are getting positively pummeled by this year’s record fuel prices, a product of America’s latest “dumb oil war” in Iran.

And, after Workhorse’ fleet logged its 20 millionth mile driven with zero tailpipe emissions, you could hardly claim that it’s an unknown quantity – a fact that Tristan understands.

“Our customers have been exploring electrification for some time now,” explains Daniel Barbu, Tristan’s Vice President and General Manager. “With generous incentives from Écocamionnage, as well as the current extremely high cost of fuel, the business case for going electric has never been stronger … we’re looking forward to helping Workhorse expand its customer base across Canada and supporting our customers meet their own goals for sustainability and vehicle performance.”

Tristan operates out of seven locations throughout Québec and Ontario. In addition to its Workhorse offerings, the company is also an authorized Michelin tire, Cummins engine, and Vanguard trailer dealer.

#4494. How Far Can Your EV Go After It Says It’s Empty?

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

What do you do when your EV’s range prediction shows zero and the nearest charger is still a few miles away? Will you make it? In a Tesla Model Y Long Range, you’d pull in with miles to spare, while in an Xpeng P7+, you’d have been on the phone with roadside assistance, even if the Xpeng goes farther on a full charge.

That’s one of the more revealing findings from AUTOBEST’s 2026 ECOBEST Challenge. All 15 EVs that took part in the group test kept moving after their dashboards showed empty, averaging 10 miles (16 km) before they stopped. The Leapmotor B10 led with 19.9 miles (32 km), about a mile ahead of the Model Y. At the other end, the Xpeng barely managed 0.6 miles.

Car journalists drove these production-spec EVs in convoy near Milan, Italy, on a set route containing a mix of city streets, country roads and highways. A lead car set the pace, and drivers traded cars every 19 miles (30 km) to level out potential differences in driving style.

Only the driver was aboard each car; all vehicles were set to their standard (not Eco) mode, with climate control on and tires set to the recommended pressures. Temperatures ranged from 68–77°F (20–25°C).

The final stretch took place at Quattroruote’s Vairano proving ground. When a car’s dashboard showed either zero remaining range or 0% battery charge, its driver kept going until the car could no longer move under its own power. They measured the distance between those two points to see how far each EV could still go.

They used a Zeekr 7GT as a support vehicle to quickly reach drivers whose EVs had stopped. Using its vehicle-to-load (V2L) function, it drew electricity from its own battery pack to get the other vehicles moving again, eliminating the need for a dedicated EV road assistance van.

When your EV says it’s empty, it means you’ve used up the range the car promised you. You may still have enough energy to drive a little farther, since all EVs have a buffer. As the state of charge goes down, the voltage in the battery cells also drops. Before it goes too low, which can damage the cells, the car cuts power to the motor.

So, even when an EV shows 0% and can’t move, some charge remains in the pack—the car won’t let it go completely flat.

Zero percent is the car’s estimate of its remaining usable charge. The range estimate approximates how far that energy will take you. Interestingly, those numbers don’t necessarily have to coincide; they can hit zero at different times. For instance, in one range test, the Tesla Model 3 still showed 2 miles (3.2 km) of range when the state of charge dropped to 0%. It went another 31 miles (50 km) after that point.

AUTOBEST published the distance each car covered after zero, but its results table doesn’t give the usable energy remaining at that moment or the speed each car maintained afterward. So we can say the Leapmotor drove 32 times as far as the Xpeng past empty, but that doesn’t mean its battery had 32 times the current reserve.

#4493. Too Much Motion in the Ocean: We Test the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450

The revised GLS-class pushes luxury to the front of the line at the cost of some composure.

You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma. And while the result of the GLS’s latest refresh largely hits the mark, we believe this ute’s ride quality missed its intended landing zone.

Let’s focus on the high points first. We’re big fans of the base GLS450’s 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six. Thanks to a stronger electric supercharger and a few other updates, this powertrain now spits out 375 horsepower and 413 pound-feet of torque fed through a nine-speed automatic transmission to all four wheels. With it, the GLS450 managed a solid 5.1-second sprint to 60, eventually clearing the quarter-mile mark in an equally respectable 13.6 seconds at 101 mph. Not bad for a gas-powered machine that tipped our scales at 5623 pounds.

See all results for used cars for sale near 60502

Out in the real world, the powertrain only ever feels smooth. Whether we’re stomping on the right pedal or just breathing on it, the result is the same: a muted little growl and plenty of grunt. The transmission stays out of the spotlight; in fact, everything hiding under the body does its best to stay out of earshot. Our microphones picked up very little cabin noise, recording just 65 decibels (20 sones) at a 70-mph cruise. Insofar as high-end family transportation goes, the GLS450 nails that part of its assignment.

The GLS450’s cabin also succeeds in its goals—mostly. The materials are standard Mercedes-Benz fare, with plenty of nice-feeling leather and vinyl up top, while most of the harder materials remain low in the cabin, away from traditional touch points. Our test car had the no-charge six-seater option; the captain’s chairs in the second row are cushy and make third-row ingress and egress a breeze. The car’s so dang large that even adults can be reasonably comfortable all the way in back, with decent headroom and legroom that’s fine for short jaunts around town.

However, our editors didn’t fully embrace the cabin’s centerpiece: the Superscreen. This panoply of digital real estate spans the entire width of the dashboard, with a single piece of glass encasing the digital gauge cluster, the primary infotainment touchscreen, and the optional (and wholly superfluous) passenger screen. It’s basically eliminated the need to design a dashboard, which does a disservice to those who appreciate an aesthetic other than Blade Runner Dystopia. In fact, this pixel addiction is a growing problem across the entire Mercedes lineup. But hey, at least the steering wheel picked up a physical rocker and a thumbwheel.

See all results for used cars for sale near 60502

When it comes to the external half of the GLS-class’s refresh, the whole look gels, but like the revised S-class sedan before it, we’re wondering if Mercedes is going too hard in the paint on the self-branding. In addition to the gigantic three-pointed star on the grille, the grille itself now contains dozens of little three-pointed stars. Each headlight now has two three-pointed stars acting as running lights. In total, the rear lights contain six three-pointed stars. It’s a great design if you’re constantly forgetting what car you bought. Who are they trying to sell this thing to, the protagonist from Memento?

The GLS450’s more prominent bugbear is its ride quality. Ordinarily, a plush ride means road inconsistencies disappear, replaced with a body that floats serenely over juts and ruts without transmitting undue movement to the cabin and its occupants. In the GLS450, though, it appears the suspension engineers were tasked with reinventing body-on-frame jiggle from first principles. On any road that isn’t obsidian smooth, the GLS suffers from an awful lot of lateral wobbling after tackling a bump, and the body barely settles down by the time the next one arrives. It’s as if the engineers benchmarked an unladen F-350. Our test car was riding on the stock air suspension, and while it’s possible that upgrading to the electrohydraulic E-Active Body Control system would eliminate these unwanted movements, we’re let down that this setup ever left the plant in Alabama.

Despite a terminal case of the Wibbly-Wobblies, GLS450 proved surprisingly sticky around our 300-foot skidpad. We managed 0.92 g of lateral grip from the Pirelli P Zero PZ5 summer tires (285/40R-23 front, 325/35R-23 rear). The GLS also stopped from 70 mph in a tidy 154 feet. We’d appreciate these stats more if they didn’t come attached to a four-wheeled waterbed.

As if it wasn’t obvious from its segment positioning, the Mercedes GLS is an expensive proposition. It starts at $95,500, and you do get a good amount of standard equipment, including heated and ventilated front seats, air springs, all-wheel drive, and the Superscreen. Our test car picked up several add-ons—including $1620 for real leather and $3300 for the AMG Line design package—ballooning the price to $113,670. There’s a lot to like about the refreshed 2027 GLS450; we just wish ride quality was on that list.

#4492. MENANCE Adds XCOM-Style Campaign in Latest Update

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

When adding new content to an early access title, developers often need to strike a balance between addressing player feedback and slotting in planned additions. When done properly, adding both can not only move a game toward its final form, but also squash bugs and hiccups that they didn’t even notice without a wide player base to catch them.

MENACE is one such indie early access darling that’s been an absolute gem to follow, providing XCOM-style combat with MechWarrior flair, a beautiful fusion of grounded, high-stakes combat.

The newest Honkai title by HoYoverse is approaching its final beta test, giving players a larger taste of its auto-battler combat.

In their most recent update, the team at Overhype Studio has implemented a mountain of fixes, as well as an XCOM Long War-style extended campaign, slowing down progression to force players into a proper test of endurance on their path to victory.

MENACE has defined itself through gritty combat and long-form tactical planning, making it a perfect follow-up from the team that developed Battle Brothers. In addition to the new campaign options, the update adds two more squadmates to join the crew, Kubra Oztok and Clay Fleetwood.

While Kubra is a super solid frontliner, with the ability to deal great mental and physical damage to enemy units, Clay is a very funny special case, being a simulation expert with no actual physical combat experience.

Rather than having a normal HP value, Clay is a long-range powerhouse who will flee instantly upon taking any form of damage. He’ll also hightail it if the battle is going poorly enough, making him a ‘win more’ addition to the team more than anything.

MENACE keeps up a great tone of realistic action and drama by balancing it with genuinely funny bits, a hard duo act to perform but one that pays off immensely. In the same way that horror and comedy are shockingly intertwined, allowing players to come up for air with a good joke or two makes it easier to take the whole setting seriously.

MENACE is one such indie early access darling that’s been an absolute gem to follow, providing XCOM-style combat with MechWarrior flair, a beautiful fusion of grounded, high-stakes combat.

All this new content comes with a facelift and small additions to make the game look and run better, including an internal error log to help diagnose hiccups or crashes, even if they stem from mods. Now that’s an addition I’d kill for in a lot of heavily moddable games, and by prepping it this early, MENACE is making the world much easier for vanilla and modded fans alike.

MENACE is a title that really feels like it has a bright future thanks to the great work from the team behind it and the incredibly passionate community it has already established. When a blog post ends with a series of community-made guides being shouted out by the devs, it really feels like the title is going places.

Thanks to early access, MENACE has opened one of the most effective developer/community pipelines I’ve ever seen, avoiding the age-old scramble of launching a game and pivoting to fix community complaints after launch by stomping them out now and encouraging the hunt for more. With a strong Very Positive on Steam and more reviews flying in every day, the players clearly like what they see.

As outwardly popular as Mechs are, it's hard to find titles that really sell their weight. While Gundam-style humanoid dash machines are always fun, getting a long-form game focusing on the big industrial stomper kind of mech is a real diamond in the rough. MENACE is a title that knows what it wants to be, is willing to shift for player feedback, and is focused on how it wants to expand despite its incredibly solid current offerings. As long as the team stays on course, it's sure to be a hit.

STJV, a French union representing members of Arkane Lyon, accuses Microsoft of major interference with the project.

#4491. Yamaha’s new electric scooter takes aim at Europe’s 125cc commuters

Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter lineup with the new XENTER E, a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter designed specifically with European city riding in mind.

Unveiled around EICMA 2026 in Milan alongside the new NMAX E, the XENTER E is a high-wheel scooter riding on 16-inch wheels front and rear.

That’s an important distinction in European cities, where larger wheels can make quick work of the cobblestones, potholes, and tram tracks that can turn smaller-wheeled scooters into teeth-rattling experiences.

The XENTER E uses Yamaha’s new eAxle powertrain, combining the motor, controller, and reduction gearbox into a compact frame-mounted unit. The motor produces 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power and 33.3 Nm of torque, putting the scooter into Europe’s A1 license category.

Mounting the motor to the frame also means Yamaha can use a more conventional motorcycle-style swingarm rather than hanging the motor on the rear suspension like many scooters. That reduces unsprung weight and should help improve handling and ride quality.

Power is supplied from an integrated 3.5 kWh battery mounted low in the chassis. Yamaha claims 108 km (67 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, though real-world range is expected to be somewhat lower.

An 800W onboard charger can refill the battery in around 5.5 hours from a public charging station. Yamaha will also offer a cable for charging from a household outlet.

Other niceties include three riding modes, traction control, regenerative braking, a reverse mode for maneuvering at low speeds, smart-key operation, and a 5-inch TFT display. Smartphone connectivity adds navigation, battery information, maintenance reminders, and parking-location tracking.

There’s also enough underseat storage for a full-face helmet, depending on its size, plus USB-C charging and provisions for accessories such as a windscreen and 34-liter top case.

The XENTER E shares its powertrain and battery with Yamaha’s new NMAX E, but the high-wheel layout gives it a distinctly more European commuter flavor.

Yamaha hasn’t officially announced pricing for each market, though early reports from Milan point to €7,799 in Germany. Deliveries are expected to begin in spring 2027.

It’s certainly not cheap, but the XENTER E looks like Yamaha is finally getting serious about building electric scooters that can replace its bread-and-butter 125cc urban machines, rather than simply supplement them.

#4490. Toyota Quietly Gave The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV A Big Upgrade

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Toyota has quietly upgraded the sixth-generation RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid. All trims of the model year 2027 RAV4 PHEV now get a Tesla-style North American Charging Standard (NACS) port straight from the factory—plus fast-charging capability.

That’s a pretty big deal for a few key reasons. When the RAV4 PHEV launched last year, it arrived with a CCS charging port at a time when all new EVs had started transitioning to native NACS ports. At the time, only the PHEV XSE and Woodland trims could fast charge, meaning you had to pay at least a $4,000 premium for the capability.

Now that fast-charging capability expands to the full PHEV lineup, all the way down to the entry SE model, which costs $42,100. The same goes for the top-trim GR Sport. Owners can now simply drive the 2027 RAV4 PHEV to Tesla Superchargers or any of the new stations equipped with NACS cables. It will charge at maximum rate of 50 kilowatts, enough to go from 10-80% in just 30 minutes.

Moreover, not many PHEVs get fast-charging capability, let alone native NACS ports. The RAV4 PHEV is now the first and only major PHEV in the U.S. to transition to the NACS port, joining the wave of new fully electric models doing the same.

Some other notable PHEVs that have fast-charging capability include the Mercedes GLC 350e which gets a CCS port and the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV which gets the outdated CHAdeMO connector.

If owners are used to plugging-in at home, they can continue to do so. The RAV4 PHEV gets an onboard AC charger for Level 1 and Level 2 charging. And home charging can now be faster as well, with GR Sport and SE trims getting 11 kW AC charging, up from 7 kW before. The XSE and Woodland were already rated for 11 kW since last year.

And the one final notable upgrade is that the charging port is now located near the driver’s side door—it was previously at the passenger’s side. This could be useful depending on how you park at home and where you live, since there’s no industry standard for the charging port location.

The newer V4 Tesla Superchargers, as well as Ionna, Walmart, and pretty much every major new station have long cables with well-engineered retraction systems, so the location of the port shouldn’t be a problem. The older V3 Tesla Superchargers will be a challenge since they were designed for rear left ports.

The RAV4 PHEV gets up to 52 miles of EPA range from its 22.7 kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery. If you regularly plug it in, you can cover your everyday driving needs using battery power alone and use the gas engine for longer trips. And now, it looks like that charging experience just got a little better.

#4489. Lincoln Is Bringing Back the Plug-In Hybrid Aviator in China

Lincoln is launching a new plug-in hybrid Aviator SUV in China, but we don’t expect to ever see it sold stateside.

Lincoln used to sell the Aviator SUV with an optional plug-in hybrid powertrain, but it was dropped from the lineup after 2023. Now, there’s a new Aviator PHEV in town, only this time, the towns it will be driving in will exclusively be across the Pacific Ocean. This is the Lincoln Aviator EX8, designed specifically for China and revealed via a regulatory filing with China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT).

Developed as part of Ford’s joint venture with Chinese automaker Changan, the new Aviator EX8 looks completely different from the Aviator SUV sold on our shores. It’s handsome and confident, with a blockier shape and an upright front end, and the large rectangular grille is adorned with a series of cascading chrome trim pieces. A large U-shaped trim piece spans the base of the front fascia, giving the SUV a planted look. It’s about the same size as the Aviator sold here, coming in a tad shorter, about an inch narrower, and roughly an inch taller. The rear is simple, with just a full-width rectangular taillight.

See all results for used Lincoln for sale near 06604

The EX8 is motivated by a plug-in hybrid powertrain. It uses a 1.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine from Changan that produces 148 horsepower, but the MIIT documents didn’t reveal any details on the number of electric motors, their positioning, or their output. In 2025, Changan launched a range-extender PHEV SUV called the Nevo Q07, which comes in single- and dual-motor configurations with up to 389 hp and a total range of 870 miles.

The Aviator EX8 is expected to get its proper reveal at the Guangzhou auto show later this month before going on sale in China next year. We can pretty definitively say that the Aviator EX8 will never be sold in the U.S., but we hope to see a hybrid Aviator return to our shores at some point in the future.

#4488. Harbinger scores another $240M in latest investment round

Electric truck maker Harbinger has been racking up wins in recent months, and after scoring a $300 million order from international shipping giant FedEx and a defense contract with the US military, the company has drummed up another $240 million in Series D funding.

Companies like FedEx and Amazon have been making serious moves to fully electrify their fleet operations, both in an effort to decarbonize and to avoid the every-increasing price of diesel. At $300 million for 2,000 medium-duty electric delivery trucks, Harbinger’s latest deal with FedEx is believed to be one of the largest binding orders for electric medium or heavy-duty trucks in history – and it’s a big enough deal to inspire more than 240 million votes of confidence in the company’s future, one dollar at a time.

“Harbinger exists to challenge what industry has learned to accept, and reinvent the critical systems the world depends on,” said John Harris, the Co-Founder and CEO of Harbinger. “By rethinking critical systems from first principles, we aim to unlock better performance, greater reliability, safer operations, and more room to grow. Electrification is at the core of everything we do, and increasingly, electrification is at the core of industry, defense, mobility, and AI. Harbinger’s role is not simply to give customers another option. It is to reset expectations for what critical systems should deliver.”

Harbinger’s Series D funding round was co-led by Tiger Global, the Capricorn Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. The company says the new funding will support expansion into energy storage systems, power generation, autonomy software, and defense applications, as well as the continued ramp up of its medium-duty platform manufacturing capacity. With this latest round of financing, Harbinger has raised over $650 million since 2021.

As for me, I’m hoping they use the money to come up with more fun, high-octane chase videos that show off their trucks’ performance capabilities. Time will tell.

#4487. EV Buyers Could Foot The Bill For Saving Europe’s Carmakers

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Buying a European EV can come with a potentially expensive catch. Policymakers want more of the batteries powering Europe’s electric cars to be made locally, helping secure jobs and reduce dependence on China. But those batteries cost more to produce, and someone has to cover the difference. It will likely be the buyer.

That’s the warning in a September 22 policy brief from Brussels think tank Bruegel, which was picked up by Euronews. The report argues that protecting established manufacturers risks leaving consumers (and taxpayers) with the bill.

Its battery calculation is pretty straightforward. Requiring EU-made cells could raise costs from €50 to €85 per kilowatt-hour. Multiply that by 60 kWh, and it works out to €2,100. A proposed low-carbon steel requirement could add another €200. Simplifying vehicle approval, meanwhile, would save manufacturers an estimated €61 per car, according to the report.

Volkswagen Group PowerCo Battery plant in Salzgitter, Germany.

None of this is set in stone, though, and what buyers would actually end up paying depends on the final form of the rules, government subsidies, and how much of the extra cost carmakers pass on to consumers. Regardless of the details, those looking to buy at the most affordable end of the market would be hit hardest.

The pressure to protect Europe’s industry is real. EU car production has fallen 19% since 2019, while buyers purchased 2.2 million fewer new cars in 2025 than in 2019. The wider automotive sector employs around 14 million people. However, Bruegel also points to continued exports and roughly €3 billion in quarterly investment in battery and EV factories. It raises concerns that Europe is gradually losing technology, suppliers, and overseas customers.

We saw this at the Paris motor show this year, where Chinese brands brought compelling software, luxurious gadget-filled interiors, and advanced charging technology, while European manufacturers leaned heavily on their history and design. The BMW iX3 and Mercedes’ electric GLC showed that Europe can fight back, but a familiar badge doesn’t sell cars as easily as it used to.

Local battery production is a hugely important component, but it’s proving difficult to set up in Europe. Northvolt’s failure, Porsche’s retreat from manufacturing at Cellforce, and shelved ACC factories show how hard it is to match China’s costs. Even batteries made in Europe often rely on equipment and know-how from Asia.

Europe’s additional duties on Chinese EVs, which can be as high as 35.3%, targeted fully electric cars while excluding plug-in hybrids. Bruegel points to flattening BEV imports from China while hybrid imports surge. It also cites French research that found EVs excluded from purchase subsidies suffered a 60% sales decline relative to eligible models, potentially slowing overall adoption and strongly suggesting that subsidies matter.

Bruegel says agreeing with China to temporarily limit the number of electric cars and plug-in hybrids sent to Europe could help. That would give European carmakers more time to develop cheaper EVs. The deal would have a clear end date, and restrictions could tighten if China broke it.

But with fewer Chinese cars available, they could end up costing more. Europe previously limited Japanese car imports, and Canada now limits Chinese EV imports. Both show the trade-off: protecting local carmakers can make cars more expensive for buyers.

Foreign investment can help Europe catch up, the report's authors argue. South Korean firms already own 65% of its battery cell manufacturing capacity, and Chinese companies own 55% of the capacity currently under construction. European factories need that outside expertise to function.

#4486. Mattel Brick Shop Launches Hot Wheels–Sized Model Car Sets

Building on the fun of its larger sets, these little brick-built cars cost less than five bucks.

Mattel’s Brick Shop only launched a year ago but has since gone from strength to strength in putting out a varied lineup of models for every enthusiast. Want a huge, blue-chip collectible Mercedes-Benz 300SL set that you can spend hours putting together? Done. Feeling a pang of nostalgia for the teal Honda Civic that got you through the college years to your first job? Sure thing, here’s one that you can swap out the wheels on.

Most of the reason the Brick Shop team has managed to get the rollout right with a mix of obvious heroes like the Lamborghini Miura and secret-enthusiast-handshake cars like the Audi RS2 is down to close work with the designers at Hot Wheels. Located in El Segundo, California, the Hot Wheels team members are all gearheads of one flavor or another, and the passion they have for all wheeled things is genuine. Just, you know, scaled down for those iconic orange tracks.

See all results for used cars for sale near 97008

Small scale is where you’ll find the latest Mattel Bricks sets, now built to the same size as the roughly 1/64th scale Hot Wheels themselves. They’re simple little cars, fewer than 30 pieces per kit, and at $4.99 each, they’re as dangerously tempting as an open family-size bag of potato chips. You can’t just have one.

The launch sets include a 2018 Audi TT RS, a 1991 Acura NSX, a 2024 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1, a Maserati MCPura, a 1999 Honda S2000, and a Bone Shaker (a 20-year-old hot rod by Hot Wheels design legend Larry Wood). The sets will be sold in blind boxes, so you’ll be getting a car at random when you’re buying them, adding to the fun. Even better is that these six tiny cars are only the first wave. By the end of next year, Mattel plans to have 20 models of 1/64-scale cars, making getting the full lineup something of a challenge for collectors. Even if you’re less serious about completing the series, one or two of these things are surely going to “accidentally” fall into the cart when you next go shopping for groceries.

#4485. Tesla deemed liable for fraud after Solar Roof ‘experiment’ on a home

A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the company repeatedly failed to hand over evidence. Tesla had already admitted it breached the contract, broke its warranty, and was negligent on the job.

The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.

The case is Conroy v. Tesla, filed in 2022 in San Diego Superior Court’s North County division (case No. 37-2022-00043670). Electrek reviewed the court orders, the complaint, and the parties’ joint trial readiness report. Here’s what’s in them.

Ambrose Conroy, who lives in Rancho Santa Fe, signed up for a Tesla Solar Roof in March 2020. The original contract was $82,210 for a 13.1 kW system. By February 2021, after two amendments, it had grown to roughly $110,000 for an 18.2 kW roof and six Powerwalls.

The roof was never finished. It never passed a county inspection, and it never produced a single kWh for the house.

Tesla isn’t contesting most of that anymore. In the joint report filed by both sides last month, Tesla stipulated to liability on three of the five claims.

The other two claims, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, are where things went badly for Tesla.

Judge Cynthia Freeland sanctioned Tesla twice over discovery before going further. She ordered it to pay $15,467.50 in February and another $13,500 in June, both times for failing to produce a proper privilege log and responsive documents, and both times warning that issue sanctions could follow.

Tesla missed the next deadline anyway. So on September 11, the court deemed Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation, limiting the trial on those claims to compensatory and punitive damages.

The judge found “ample evidence to support that Defendants have acted willfully.” Among the missing records were Microsoft Teams messages (Tesla’s own corporate witness testified they’re kept “for infinity”), OSHA logs, emails with San Diego County inspectors, and more than 20 quality, install, and safety reports from Tesla’s internal Bolt system.

Tesla asked her to reconsider, arguing it had since produced everything. She said no in a ruling dated October 27, writing that the late documents could support Conroy’s theory that Tesla “knowingly used Plaintiff’s home as an experiment while knowing they lacked the experience to perform as promised.”

And the “experiment” word shows up in Tesla’s own messages, according to the trial exhibit list. Exhibit 224 is described as text messages from January 13, 2021, between Tesla’s director of model engineering Bobby Yang and other Tesla employees.

To be clear, that’s how Conroy’s side describes the messages on the exhibit list. We haven’t seen the texts themselves. But Elon Musk is on Conroy’s witness list, and internal emails quoted in the complaint point the same way.

On February 9, 2021, Yang wrote internally that the house was in the “99.5 percentile in terms of complexity” and that “if we can do this job well, we should be able to do any job well.” RJ Johnson, then head of Tesla’s energy business, replied that the project would “skew numbers” but that Tesla needed “to make it right.”

Johnson was fired in April 2021. The roof had at least 59 mounting planes, and one employee called it the largest job Tesla had attempted at the time, according to the complaint.

Conroy’s account of the installation reads like a list of everything that can go wrong on a roof. These are his allegations, but Tesla has now conceded breach and negligence.

The tear-off was supposed to take two days and took two weeks. Tesla left in November 2020 with bare roof decking exposed, then had crews work overtime on December 27 to get underlayment down before a storm. Tiles arrived scratched and damaged and went on the roof anyway. Glass tiles shattered in the driveway and lawn, and the family says they still can’t walk there barefoot.

By March 2021, Johnson had agreed in writing that paying “when you’re happy with the outcome is completely reasonable.” Tesla’s billing department kept calling anyway.

In August 2021, an internal email weighed just leaving.

The project went through at least seven project managers. In November 2021, Tesla told Conroy the people behind its repair plan were gone and it had nobody in the area to do the work.

In April 2022, Tesla offered $5,000 to settle everything.

It didn’t end there. In February 2025, more than two years into the lawsuit, Tesla failed another San Diego County inspection after showing up without the plans for the venting system. And this summer, Conroy’s electrical expert opened up part of the roof and concluded that the way Tesla ran wiring and conduit under the tiles created a short-circuit and fire risk in heavy rain. The roof is now coming off. Tesla’s lawyers point out that even Conroy’s counsel called that fire risk “counterintuitive.”

Tesla is fighting the sanction hard. In an October 29 filing, it asked the court to freeze the case while it petitions the California Court of Appeal, arguing the order is “unduly punitive,” violates due process, and amounts to a directed verdict on fraud before trial.

Tesla also says the discovery fight had no connection to the fraud claims and that it has now produced everything relevant. The judge already rejected that argument once.

The November 20 trial date is off. A trial readiness conference is set for December 4, and Conroy’s lawyers want to go to trial in December.

This isn’t the first Solar Roof horror story in this case file. Conroy’s complaint attaches our 2020 report on a Solar Roof buyer left with tarps over his house after Tesla tried an untested underlayment on his home. It also cites a 2025 California Contractors State License Board action seeking to revoke Tesla’s contractor licenses over abandoned Solar Roof jobs.

What a nightmare. This is the most damaging Solar Roof case I’ve seen, and I’ve been covering this product since Elon Musk unveiled it on a Universal Studios backlot in 2016.

A botched install isn’t news on its own. Tesla only installed about 3,000 of these roofs before killing the product this year, and plenty of them went sideways. What’s different here is the paper trail: internal emails calling a customer’s home a test of whether Tesla could do “any job,” texts describing the job as an “experiment” with daily reports going to Musk, and then years of Tesla failing to hand over its own records until a judge ran out of patience.

And Tesla’s response to all of it was $5,000.

Look, it’s normal for things not to go as planned with a new product, and early adopters need to be flexible. However, we are talking about someone’s literal roof over their head here and a trillion-dollar company. Tesla could have and should have made it right a long time ago.

I suspect that by the time this is all said and done, how many ever years that is from now, it would be cheaper for Tesla to hand over a 2.5M$ check to the family. This feels like it's going long battle and they've already started spending on lawyers with more to come. And even if by some miracle Tesla wins the fraud part, they've already agreed to breach of contract, etc which is going to cost them significantly.

The issue sanction might not survive the Court of Appeal. Courts don’t love deciding fraud through discovery orders, and Tesla’s due process argument isn’t frivolous. But even if it gets reversed, Tesla has still admitted it breached the contract and was negligent, and the jury will see how this customer was treated.

This also says a lot about how Tesla ran the Solar Roof business. It sold a product it knew was hard to install, on homes it knew were complex, while the people running the program kept leaving. Conroy’s house was one of the worst cases, but installers are still dealing with the fallout of Tesla walking away from the product earlier this year.

The real question is what’s in those Teams messages and texts Tesla fought so hard to keep out of this case. If this goes to trial in December, we might find out.

#4484. 2027 Toyota RAV4 Raises Prices and Ride Height, PHEV Model Adds NACS

The 2027 RAV4 Woodland gets a new suspension system that gives it an additional inch of ground clearance.

The 2027 Toyota RAV4 arrives with a collection of small tweaks that should add up to real improvements. Unfortunately, though not surprisingly, the new model year also comes with a slight price bump.

The 2027 RAV4 starts at $33,895 in front-drive LE trim, $36,695 for the front-drive SE, and $38,095 for the front-drive XLE Premium. Adding all-wheel drive to any of those trims incurs an additional $1600 cost. The AWD-only Woodland trim is up to $42,250, while the XSE is up to $43,495, and the Limited is up to $45,495. Pricing for the plug-in versions starts at $43,695 for the entry SE, $47,650 for the Woodland, $49,395 for the XSE, and $50,695 for the GR Sport.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota RAV4 for sale near 37167

Every RAV4 thankfully now comes with a backup camera washer, and every AWD RAV4 gets Toyota’s Multi-Terrain Select modes. Plus, the Remote Connect trial is increasing from one year to five years, no matter the trim.

The bigger changes come when you zoom in. Woodland versions get redesigned all-weather floor and cargo mats. They also come with new suspension components, including springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, that give them an additional inch of ground clearance. The granola-munching RAV4 now has 9.1 inches of clearance, compared with 8.1 inches for the rest of the lineup (aside from the GR Sport).

The plug-in models get some real changes, too. For starters, all PHEV RAV4s now come with a NACS charging port and a subsequent upgrade to Level 3 DC fast-charging. Interestingly, the switch to NACS resulted in Toyota relocating the charge port to the driver’s side of the vehicle. Plus, the onboard charger has been upgraded to a maximum of 11 kW on every trim.

The first of the standard hybrid models will start arriving later this year, with plug-in models scheduled to launch in early 2027.

#4483. 10 Biggest Reveals From Final Fantasy 14's Tokyo Fanfest

Stephanie Watel is a writer for DualShockers. She has 3 years of experience writing about video games, from news to lists to in-depth guides.

To be perfectly candid, Final Fantasy XIV’s Tokyo leg of the Fanfest circuit ahead of Evercold was a surreal and almost puzzling experience. Most of the expansion’s biggest surprises were already spoiled in both Anaheim and Berlin, while Tokyo essentially served as a clarity-and-elaboration session for much of what we already knew in a basic sense.

However, that isn’t to say that director Naoki (“Yoshi-P”) Yoshida’s keynote wasn’t full of impressively dense information for players to soak in. There was a lot to go around, to the point that Yoshi-P went almost 30 minutes past his allotted runtime for the presentation, on top of saying that it originally came out to almost four hours during rehearsal. That still doesn’t even include the “several” Producer Live Letter streams he also has planned leading up to Evercold’s launch to go over everything even further.

Square Enix veteran Koji Fox says lead writer Natsuko Ishikawa is snowed under and off-limits.

If anything, it’s a perfect metaphor for just how dramatically different Evercold is actually set to be, compared to all previous expansions in the game. Most of the game’s major content is getting a systemic overhaul, and those changes branch out even further, down to some of the smallest details. It’s almost on par with A Realm Reborn’s aptly named “rebirth” of the entire game over a decade ago, without having to shut the entire game down for nearly a year.

All that said, Tokyo Fanfest had plenty of information for players to take with them, and here are the biggest reveals from the entire keynote.

Evercold dropping in the dead of winter in January was poetically on point, and up through Berlin’s Fanfest we’ve known that Final Fantasy 14’s latest and most ambitious expansion yet was set to kick off a busy year for gamers (with the likes of Fable and Final Fantasy 7: Revelation also set for early Spring).

However, at the top of Yoshi-P’s keynote in Tokyo, he announced with regret that Evercold has gotten a three-week delay to late February. Now the expansion will debut on February 23, 2027, with a special Early Access period for those who pre-order starting on February 19.

As for why this is the case, Yoshi-P explained that, initially, Evercold would have been “barely” ready to go in time for their original January release deadline, which going by a three-week delay means that the expansion would have arrived at the tail end of month. However, due to “several issues” they encountered during development, Yoshi-P made the executive decision to impose the delay to ensure those problems are properly resolved before launch.

Despite this, the delay hasn’t impacted when players will get to preorder Evercold, and you can do so for all platforms starting November 4, 2026. Ultimately, given just how much is changing in the game systemically with Evercold, it’s just as well that this delay happened, and January did seem a bit ambitious already. Nonetheless, the rock isn’t getting kicked too far down the street, and the expansion will be in players’ hands soon enough.

On the heels of Evercold’s amended release date announcement, Yoshi-P pivoted straight to the grand reveal of the expansion’s second new combat job. Granted, there was strong speculation already after the many hints dropped at Berlin’s Fanfest that it revolved around something akin to a Hunter or a Falconer, and it was already confirmed that it would be a physical ranged DPS.

Finally, all the theory crafting was laid to rest with the reveal of Zephyr, courtesy of Visna posing as the job’s mascot. As shown in the active demonstration video, the player wields a crossbow weapon while flanked by a magical falcon familiar known as a Nephele. The video displayed various combat abilities, from basic attacks with the crossbow to more striking, magic-imbued ones that have your work together with your falcon to produce some spectacular moves.

What’s more, during a Q&A session on the second day of Tokyo’s Fanfest, Yoshi-P answered a fan’s question about being able to customize your bird companion. It turns out that you actually can thanks to a dual-dye system that allows you to recolor the bird when visiting a “certain NPC” in the game.

While FF14 players knew that changes to gear would be inevitable with Evercold’s new activity system, Yoshi-P surprised just about everyone during the keynote with sweeping alterations to raid gear in particular.

While Seasonal Gear is intended for “everyday” players with a simple optimization routine, Raid Gear comes with a few different new details. The first and most surprising change is that every single person in a raid group will now get their own personal chest drop after completing the duty, rather than having the group roll the dice on a single chest once a week. This will make raiding significantly more efficient (especially for premade groups or “statics”) in lieu of having to farm several runs just for the sake of gearing everyone up for the next raid.

Alongside that, players will also get to edit the “secondary attributes” of raid gear, allowing them to personally customize how their earned gear performs rather than just being stuck with preset attributes. Also, the item level of Raid Gear can be raised twice, and materia slots will unlock upon reaching that maximum item level.

Yoshi-P went into explicit detail in this section of the keynote to explain exactly how the gear upgrading process will work, and while it felt somewhat like a labyrinth of steps and stat numbers, it nonetheless looks like a promising move in the right direction for the game’s raid community in general.

The core that’s tying mostly everything together in Evercold’s revamped gameplay is the all-new Activity Level system. The Berlin keynote gave a soft introduction to this system with a basic explanation of weekly missions that will replace Final Fantasy 14’s traditional daily duties.

During the Tokyo keynote, Yoshi-P tied that back in with the introduction of the Activity Level system, which is how all players will obtain their Seasonal Gear throughout each “season” of the expansion’s patch cycle. As you complete Missions from the long list of available options, you’ll earn Activity Points that in turn raise your Activity Level. As that level goes up, you’ll gradually unlock rewards for your efforts, ranging from gil to emotes to mounts, and then so-called “gear categories”.

Unlocking these gear categories allows you to receive gear pieces of that category (e.g. - accessories) for your jobs. Furthermore, each category is shared across all jobs, so you don’t have to worry about your alt jobs missing out on those rewards. Redeeming those gear rewards is also done via the game’s new character UI dashboard.

Up to this point, the basic understanding that we have about our journey on the Fourth is that most of it will occur on the planet’s Fimm Himnar realmships, or the “Five Firmaments Left to Mankind”. These absolutely massive realmships each pertain to a different element and a certain sector of produced resources that can’t otherwise be obtained on the frozen surface.

Back in the Berlin Fanfest, Yoshi-P provided a detailed look at two of these realmships. One was Naglfar, the Realmship of Water where Visna resides. The other was Hringhorni, the Realmship of Fire where we now know that Bastion-wielding Baldr serves as its foreman.

Here's everything you need to know Final Fantasy XIV Evercold, from new characters, new factions, and how we're able to travel to different shards.

This time around, in-depth looks were provided for two more of these realmships. One was the Realmship of Earth, Sessrymnir, and a walkthrough video gave insight into the ship’s agriculture and mining production areas. Meanwhile, the Realmship of Wind, Skidbladnir, was also shown off in all its glory. Not only is it where the ridiculously adorable Kottr live, but it’s where they work on the production of airships, the main method of transportation on the Fourth.

The fifth and final realmship remains a mystery, which is likely for the sake of story spoilers, and it also remains to be seen what other explorable areas there may be. After all, a traditional Final Fantasy XIV expansion normally has at least six major zones that players can freely navigate, and the five realmships leave at least one of those zones in limbo. The closest guess would be somewhere on the subzero surface of the Fourth, but players will have to wait and see in February.

Alliance Raids aren’t just getting a new collaboration with Neon Genesis Evangelion for Evercold, they’re also getting their own systemic overhaul for the new expansion and beyond. These changes, according to Yoshi-P, reflect a few overarching issues that the content has suffered from over past expansions.

These issues start with skewed runtimes for the game’s entire roster of Alliance Raids. Some are generally more “efficient” to run, while others (e.g. - Tower of Paradigm’s Reach) are notoriously long and thus considered not optimal for dailies, leveling, farming gear, what have you. This gaping divide in runtime has since led to a bias within the player community, and leaves certain Alliance Raids infamously difficult to queue for, much less actually complete.

However, Yoshi-P has sought out a solution in the form of subdividing Alliance Raids into two instanced chunks. The first chunk will consist of the overall raid’s first two bosses (with trash mobs in between), while the second chunk will be the final two bosses in the same fashion. After completing the first half and obtaining your rewards from it, you’ll then be able to queue separately at your own discretion for the second half, complete it, and earn separate rewards from that chunk.

This is to help alleviate the burden of farming endlessly for certain gear items over the course of a 30 minute to 1 hour raid instance, all while also being able to enjoy the content more feasibly with less of a time commitment. Furthermore, Yoshi-P hinted at not having to roll anymore for loot from these raids, with a promise to elaborate more on that closer to Evercold’s launch.

Finally, Alliance Raids get one more big update starting in Evercold in the form of a legitimate “Savage” mode. Influenced by the success of Variant and Criterion Dungeon content, this will be an 8-player mode, rather than the usual lineup of 24 WoLs, and will function more as a boss rush-style instance with two bosses from the original raid set at “Savage Turn 3”-level difficulty. This mode will kick off with Evercold’s Evangelion collaboration raid series.

While many of the game’s existing combat modes are getting their own unique changes, there’s also an entirely new type of combat content debuting during Evercold called the Gauntlet of Power.

As its name suggests, it’s a gauntlet-style instance that functions as a more casual (compared to Alliance Raid Savage, at least) boss rush for players to embark on at their leisure. That is to say, it’s a mode that can be easily accessed from almost anywhere via the game’s overhauled UI. It can be played either with a premade group or a random queue, in much the same fashion as other instanced duties in the game.

This boss rush consists of up to five “floors” for a light party group, and clearing each floor leads to rewards that weren’t yet revealed during the keynote. Players can vote whether or not to continue the gauntlet, which provides a flexibility that not many of the other types of battle content in the game have. Despite being simple in concept, it may very well help bridge a gap that’s been lingering in Final Fantasy’s 14 gameplay flow for several years.

What’s more, this mode will help keep things interesting by choosing from an assortment of 200 different existing bosses in the game. This assures that the mode will traditionally prevalent issue of content monotony as much as possible while maintaining a sense of liberty and gratification for the player to make the most of their time.

Another big surprise that Yoshi-P was surprisingly candid about during Tokyo Fanfest’s Q&A session is that Allagan Tomestones of Poetics, the currency that’s remained in the game the longest (aside from maybe MGP), is set to officially retire in Evercold.

Yoshi-P did say that he shouldn’t really be discussing it just yet, but did confirm the plan nonetheless. He did offer a brief explanation in that “there will be something that allows you to trade for gear for alt jobs, or past rewards; you don’t have to worry about it for now. It just won’t be Poetics anymore.”

For players who have been in Final Fantasy 14 for at least some amount of time, Allagan Tomestones has since become the fall-back currency for the game’s more niche purchases. Alternatively, you could redeem them for one of the game’s more recent variants of tomestone currencies. Beyond A Realm Reborn, Poetics lose much of their remaining purpose, and at this point they feel more like a souvenir that just collects dust from one expansion to the next.

However, on that note, with the game’s dramatic revamp to the Activity Points system and Seasonal Gear, it remains to be seen if other tomestone currencies, such as those we had in Dawntrail, will keep some sort of utility themselves. Yoshi-P hasn’t been abundantly clear on just how long tomestone currency will hang on for, and if it will perhaps deviate to some other set purpose in the game. Otherwise, Evercold may be the “poetic” farewell to tomestone currency across the board as we know it.

While not necessarily anything to do with the game’s many different content systems, the keynote did get a small update on the story front in the form of identity reveals for certain characters. Baldr, the one wielding Bastion gear in the trailer, was revealed as the foreman of the Hringhorni realmship. Meanwhile, an entirely new face appeared in the final version of the trailer that ironically looked very familiar to many fans.

The presentation revealed her as Lagertha, the first mate of the Naglfar realmship where Visna resides. However, beyond finding out her purpose on the ship, fans are moreso scratching their heads over her striking resemblance to Ysayle, a key character who tragically passed during the events of Heavensward and the Dragonsong War.

However, players with a sharp eye may have caught the glimpse of her during the final Dawntrail MSQ content in Patch 7.56, meaning that her appearance is no coincidence. The most likely explanation for her presence on the Fourth is that Lagertha is her reflection. As to how deeply her character will impact the story of Evercold, players will simply have to wait and look forward to it.

On another non-combat tangent, Final Fantasy 14’s ever-controversial housing system is getting more bells and whistles added to it with Evercold’s patch cycle. Those changes are spread across “three pillars”, as indicated in the presentation.

First off, as hinted over the past several months, all houses will get an “interior area size customization” feature. This means that, for example, you can customize the interior of your small house to have the layout of a large house, for a currently undisclosed gil fee. Not only that, the furnishing limit will flex according to the layout you choose, so there’s no need to worry about getting cut off on your desired decor.

Secondly, floating interior furnishings will no longer be something only achievable through unconventional PC glitching controls. Along with an all-new placement interface, players will be able to move furnishings more freely on the vertical axis on both console and PC platforms.

The third and final pillar consists of adding even more housing plots, though Yoshi-P noted that they’re still discussing how exactly they want to achieve that, whether it’s through more, smaller areas, “hidden” areas, et cetera. While more plots feels moreso like another bandaid to a system that itself needs an overhaul, it’s at least nice that they’re doing their best to improve what’s in place until that change hopefully comes one day.
