TYLOO's withdrawal from a HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final in Lisbon has left their PGL Major Singapore invite in doubt on cutoff day. In Europe, fnatic are shut out of the last CS2 Major of 2026 after the final weekend's results went against them.

One walkover in Lisbon looks set to decide Asia’s line-up for the PGL Major Singapore.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. 100 Thieves beat Wildcard 2-0 in Sunday’s FiRe Last Chance final, and the European VRS now places them 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 25.1.81 - Latest Addition: Branik, Liora, Kaelith, Paris, Mordred, Morgause

Arthurian legends are still really popular today, especially in video games. No wonder: with its kings, knights, fairies, and epic battles, it's a very exciting and complex story. A story that is also told in Frost & Flame: King of Avalon.

In this strategy game, you get to manage and upgrade your own castle as well as train your dragon. Dragons have special traits and abilities, all of which are useful during battles, but also for resource gathering or to develop the city.

Frost & Flame: King of Avalon also features multiplayer content, so you can join alliances to cooperate with each other... or lose battles together. Needless to say, this is a must-play for strategy and/or fantasy fans.

Aurelius Pendragon is one of the best heroes: his skills attract enemies, boost his allies' critical chance, and bless them. His Unique Skill also increases Infantry Attack. Morrigan is another strong pick, especially for players who prefer an aggressive playstyle, as her skills focus on offence. As for Orlando the Nightshard and Evaine the Bestower, they both have a skill that grants extra health in Explore battles.

Next up on our Frost & Flame: King of Avalon tier list are heroes that are still really capable, just not as much as the ones in S-tier. It's safe to use resources to upgrade them and send them to battle.

Accolon of Gaul's Unique Skill, Knight of Ice, reduces enemy Infantry's Defense, making him a good choice if your army lacks firepower. As for Elaine of Garlot and Caradoc, they're useful if your army has a large number of marksmen.

To wrap up our Frost & Flame: King of Avalon tier list, we have the weakest heroes of the game. It's fine to use them early on, but don't rely on them too much and quickly switch to better ones whenever you summon heroes from the tiers above.

Except for Sir Gaheris, all these heroes have decent firepower, but they're just not strong enough in the long run.

#4379. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

There's also a live game soundtrack concert in Los Angeles featuring Thot Squad, Bershy, Primer, Caroline Kingsbury, Fartbarf, and Dispatch composer Andrew Arcadi with the SDN Company Band. It will be held at Avalon Hollywood on December 3, but it won't be livestreamed, so you'll need to grab a ticket to see the event. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4374. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4373. Tenebris Somnia Review – A Hair-Raising And Entertaining Throwback

Tenebris Somnia channels the old-school appeal of classic point-and-click adventures, survival horror, and full-motion-video (FMV) experiences, then smartly modernizes them to create a creepy, entertaining experience. Surviving the twisted threats of a demonic dream world is a tightly packed adventure that rewards you with what’s essentially an impressive indie horror film peppered throughout. It’s a nightmare you may not want to wake up from.

The blend of live-action and in-game storytelling works well in Tenebris Somina’s adventure, which begins when protagonist Julia visits the apartment of her filmmaker ex-boyfriend, Ivan, after suffering recurring nightmares of him being massacred by monsters. What begins as a well-meaning check-in on his status spirals down an unsettling rabbit hole when Julia’s worst fears are realized and then some. The dialogue-free tale presents a scary but fascinating exploration of obsession, both in art and in romance, that constantly delivers surprising, and at times upsetting, revelations during its eight-hour runtime. While Tenebris Somnia sometimes leans a little too far into “tell, don’t show” territory when explaining the cool lore of its supernatural threats, I never felt lost or confused about the wild things that regularly unfold on screen.

FMV experiences are nothing new, but Tenebris Somnia’s live-action scenes are a highlight. They’re well shot, sport impressively gruesome practical effects, and even present visual clues that make them important to gameplay. These scenes are additive, never taking too much time away from the in-game action, and they feel well placed to elicit the strongest emotional response. I also appreciate how the live scenes fit thematically, as much of Tenebris Somnia’s tale centers on a horror film shot by Ivan and Julia that significantly impacted their former relationship; at times, it’s like watching a movie about the movie. While I enjoy smaller moments, like opening a door to trigger a live-action jump scare, the filmmaking succeeds in selling Julia's emotions and the cast's reactions. Seeing real fear, concern, and determination in Julia’s eyes as she navigates a dreamworld made up of Ivan’s memories helped endear me to what would otherwise be a featureless pixel sprite.

Gameplay may look unimpressive due to its old-school adventure game presentation, but Tenebris Somnia’s spin on familiar survival-horror mechanics hits the right notes. Taking place entirely within a dreamlike version of a four-story apartment building, you’ll traverse floors collecting and combining objects and deciphering clues to solve well-crafted puzzles. I’m impressed by how well the game’s puzzles make the most of its limited graphical presentation, including clever scenarios involving mirror/screen reflections I won’t spoil, and how consistently creative they are. One devious exercise even utilizes the game’s limited save points as an unexpected resource in a way that changes how you approach your adventure going forward. No matter how strange puzzles become, they are never opaque, requiring just enough out-of-the-box thinking to make me feel smart when I connect the dots.

Battling grotesque monsters (which, naturally, look even creepier in live-action) also feels good, with melee and gunplay sporting deliberate animations reminiscent of classic adventure games without feeling mechanically clunky. Taking on multiple enemies by swinging a pipe or blowing them away with a shotgun feels better than it looks, and the most intense encounters end just as they approach the line of becoming overwhelming.

Boss battles, perhaps most unexpectedly for a largely puzzle-focused adventure, are fun and distinct from each other, be it wave-based bouts against small gremlin-like foes, protecting a fragile effigy of yourself from a parade of demented house servants, or battling literal mirror images of a tentacled flesh monster the Resident Evil series would be proud to claim. Managing limited ammo and health strikes a good balance of feeling tense but not oppressive. Playing conservatively is rewarding, as few non-boss threats need to be engaged if you can evade them well enough. But when I did find myself down to my last bullet or on the verge of death, Tenebris Somnia lets you feel the pinch just long enough before dropping a box of bullets or a health vial at the right moment.

Tenebris Somnia mines the enjoyable nostalgia of playing the horror games of yesteryear without feeling dated in the worst way. Weaving a solid indie horror film adds to the experience rather than feeling like a gimmick. The result is a captivating, well-executed survival-horror romp that maintains a hair-raising atmosphere with a fraction of the pixels of other genre giants.

#4372. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4371. Crusaders Heaven tier list of every skin in the game

A detailed tier list of normal and exclusive skins in Crusader Heaven ranked by their effectiveness.

Crusaders Heaven is one of the best Roblox combat games based on JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure. As you play, you'll see that the exciting skins, trading system, and accessories make Crusaders Heaven interesting not only for JoJo fans but also for those who like collectables. In this article, you will find every in-game skin sorted into an impressive Crusaders Heaven tier list.

It includes normal skins available at the time of writing and limited exclusives that can be obtained only during a specific time. The tier list might come in handy not only for beginners but also for experienced players who want to expand their knowledge about Crusaders Heaven.

WHAT IS OUR CRUSADERS HEAVEN TIER LIST? The game has a comprehensive skins system, and our Crusaders Heaven tier list includes a particular Extra Tier for event-exclusive skins. They can't be obtained nowadays but are still worth a unique place in this guide.

Tier SS includes the rarest skins in Crusaders Heaven. These are a great way to stand out among other players and look completely unique. The only issue is that Tier SS skins are the rarest in Crusaders Heaven, so you might just end up spending a lot of time trying to get them.

The World: OVA The World: OVA is the most exciting skin you can get for The World stand, the main stand of Dio Brando. It's a strong stand that's most effective at close range. Using The World with OVA skin is the best way to make your character look more appealing.

Tier S still includes valuable skins. Even though getting them is a little bit more straightforward than tier SS skins, they are hard to get if you're not spending real money on the game.

Star Platinum Television Star Platinum Television is the skin for one of the most potent stands in Crusaders Heaven. Even though it only features visual improvements for your character, using Television Skin for your Star Platinum is one of the best ways to stand out among all players.

Tier A skins are way more accessible than tier SS/S skins. Using tier A skins is a great option if you want to look cool and don’t want to donate money or spend dozens of hours trying to obtain the best ones.

Star Platinum: The Galaxy The Galaxy is another skin for Star Platinum stand in Crusaders Heaven. Even though this skin is less rare than Star Platinum Television, many players still like to opt for The Galaxy instead of Television.

Tier B includes valuable skins that can be used even during later game stages. They are perfectly suitable for trading in order to get more expensive skins, as well as for wearing them just to look cool. You should never underestimate tier B skins in Crusaders Heaven.

Diego Diego, or Diego Brando, is an outfit of one of the secondary antagonists in Crusaders Heaven. Even though this skin seems pretty valuable, it belongs to Tier B. So, getting it is not a big problem even if you are a beginner.

Tier C includes the most accessible skins in Crusaders Heaven. Even though experienced players don't really appreciate outfits from tier C, they are still widely used among beginners. And if you're not a big fan, remember you can use tier C skins to trade for a better outfit.

Shiny King Crimson Shiny King Crimson is one of the most accessible skins for the King Crimson stand. It is a human-looking stand that appears slightly bigger than your character in Crusaders Heaven.

Tier E is the last tier and includes the worst skins in Crusaders Heaven. These skins have no value, which isn't surprising since most tier E skins are based on the appearance of minor characters from JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure.

Shiny Killer Queen Shiny Killer Queen is a copy of Shiny King Crimson, but for the Killer Queen stand of Kira Yoshikage in Crusaders Heaven. The only difference is that Shiny Killer Queen is more accessible, which is why it's in tier E.

The Event tier includes exclusive event stand skins that are available only during a specific time of the year. Sometimes, Event tier skins are more difficult to obtain than those in tier SS. So if you have one, you're sure to stand out from the crowd if you wear the exclusive skins from this tier.

Valentine Platinum Valentine Platinum is considered the most valuable skin for the Star Platinum stand, which will make you look unique even when compared to players with tier SS skins. The only issue is that it is nearly impossible to get Valentine Platinum nowadays.

And that's our Crusaders Heaven tier list! Keep in mind that this article is regularly updated. It always includes skins from the latest Crusaders Heaven updates, so feel free to share it with friends.

#4369. A Mass Effect 5 Trailer Featuring Liara Appears To Have Leaked Following BioWare's Closure

In case you missed the tragic news yesterday, EA laid off 400 employees this week, including all of BioWare. The studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more, has been shut down, and its last remaining project was canceled. The game in question was a fifth entry in the Mass Effect universe, and BioWare shared very little about it – not even an official name. Following the studio's closure, however, a trailer for the sci-fi sequel started circulating around the internet.

While no official BioWare representatives have confirmed that the footage is real, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier claims that it is. Schreier has a history of credible reporting in the field, and was the first to break the news about the layoffs. IGN has also stated that it confirmed the trailer's legitimacy.

If you want to see for yourself, you can watch the trailer on Reddit.

"The following is in-engine footage form our small team," text at the start of the video reads. "It uses our pre-production assets." The footage shows no gameplay, but includes a good-looking CG cutscene of a new protagonist speaking with an asari woman in a crowded bar. As he tells her about his life, we see glimpses of him as a soldier, then as some kind of spy, traveling to several planets to track down conflicts and "stopping them before they start." After the asari woman reveals that she's been "starting the fires" he's trying to prevent, another woman behind her lowers a hood. This new woman reveals herself as Liara T'Soni, one of Mass Effect's most iconic characters.

Then, Liara and the protagonist team up to take out the woman at the bar and her henchmen, using guns and telekinetic abilities. The trailer fades to black, then fades back in to reveal the game's would-be title: Mass Effect Universe. It's a great-looking trailer – it's a shame the game will never see the light of day.

With a shaky predecessor, Infinity Ward had a lot to repair and conclude, especially with 4 set to bookend the rebooted Modern Warfare series. Fortunately, backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 makes up for the past and then some.

Modern Warfare 4 continues after the events of 2023’s Modern Warfare 3, with Captain Price hellbent on stopping Makarov and his higher-ups. The story features shifting perspectives, from a new group of ragtag Korean soldiers to familiar characters like Gaz. The character dynamics harken back to the original trilogy, especially in the boots-on-the-ground missions with the South Korean unit, led by Park (played by Beef actor Young Mazino).

For a series that, at least recently, has been more spectacle than story, giving the stakes the time they deserve is nice. While it moves away from the stealthy and modernized elements, it makes sense for the matters at hand. The majority of Modern Warfare 4’s attempts at wrapping up the overarching plot of the rebooted series works, but it rushes through some character arcs and story beats in uneven fashion. Furthermore, much of the game’s cast, especially Mads Mikkelson’s Archer and Prisca Kim’s Ri Ju-Young, are underutilized, which is a shame since they both deliver great performances.

Despite the shortcomings of the campaign, Call of Duty's bread and butter, multiplayer, still delivers. While it doesn’t have the fluidity of Black Ops’ newer entries, the customization and design of weapons and maps make it worth digging into. From small, intimate shooting galleries with Mumbai and Nautical to wide free-for-alls like Coal and Reactor U92, the range helps maintain excitement, even if it gets repetitive over time.

The variety of multiplayer modes keeps things fresh on the battlefield. Returning modes like standard Team Deathmatch and Kill Confirmed continue that enjoyable competitive flair that made them the stars that they are. However, new modes like Combat Outpost and Hijack fit right into the already great lineup. In particular, Combat Outpost upscales your typical 6v6 player count to 24v24, leading to more action and teamwork. Hanging onto a team’s tank, shooting enemies from afar, and taking back outposts is exhilarating, even if it can all go bad moments later by a well-placed RPG shot.

Even after hours of gameplay, the variety of options to craft your perfect gun is impressive. Figuring out the best scope, ammo, stock, and muzzle, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them, is a fun way of customizing your playstyle. Gunny, a mechanic that helps optimize your gun for certain styles, can help with decision paralysis, but I rarely used it. Not many FPSs go that far and Modern Warfare 4’s commitment to the feature makes it stand out.

The newest mode, DMZ, impresses out of the gate. After a few flat attempts in the past, this is the definitive Call of Duty extraction shooter, whether you play solo, or in duos or trios. Immediately, you’re thrust into the wide open world of Hajin and left to fend for yourselves with what you have and what you can gather and extract. Fans of Arc Raiders and Marathon should feel right at home as the gameplay borrows from the typical extraction shooter experience. Intense, action-packed moments keep you coming back after every win or loss. And the excellent gunplay and level design elevate it into something worthwhile, no matter how you play.

Despite not encountering many live players during my time in Hajin in DMZ, it still proves challenging, even for seasoned pros. The world is not your friend, and taking risks can come at a high cost. A good team, as well as a thoughtful loadout and traits, are required to survive. The unpredictability of it all keeps you on your toes, making for an exciting addition to the already strong multiplayer suite.

Regardless of the mode, Modern Warfare 4 is one of the best-looking Call of Duty titles to date. New York and Paris are lifelike, and it truly embodies the realistic, modern aesthetic the series has always aimed to achieve. However, I encountered a few technical hiccups, especially in the campaign. Slow framerate plagues some high-octane scenes and texture loading is frequent across the board. These distractions are far from game-breaking, but enough to be noticeable.

While the plot execution is a bit shaky, engaging multiplayer options, including DMZ, aptly demonstrate that Infinity Ward can still deliver compelling military-FPS experiences. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a strong return to form that serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries.

#4363. 10 Legendary Grenades and Ordnances You Should Have in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There are various types of legendary items in Borderlands 4, and it goes without saying that they are some of the best items in the game. Because of this, you will want to fill your endgame build with legendary items galore.

The main items you will be using across your builds are weapons, shields, and grenades. Once you have some powerful legendary weapons and have acquired a shield, you will need to focus on getting either a strong grenade or a strong ordnance. For a primary weapon, consider the best legendary assault rifles.

There are numerous legendary grenades and ordnances in Borderlands 4, and several of them are must-have items at this point in the game to refine your build with.

There are some grenades that you have to be careful about where you throw them, and then there are grenades that many refer to as “throw and forget” grenades. This is because you don’t need to worry about where you throw them. Instead, you can toss it in a general direction and go.

The Swarm is a grenade you can forget about because it homes in on targets. Its ability, Swoosh, makes it spawn three homing grenades on impact, and those spawn additional homing grenades for a total of nine.

If you happen to get bonuses on this build that increase your grenade damage and explosion size, you will be living the dream. You can get the Swarm from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

If you are someone who wants to use ordnances, your options are somewhat limited, as there aren’t as many of them in the game, but they are quite powerful. One of the more powerful ones is the Disc Jockey.

This heavy launcher has the ability Bouncing Biscuits, which makes it so it launches energy discs that bounce off surfaces. Each time one of these discs bounces, the damage of the disc increases by 20%.

This is a weapon that is great in small rooms, as the bounces can rack up some serious damage on groups of enemies. You can get this weapon from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

It is interesting whenever a grenade doesn’t deal grenade damage and instead gets all its power from another source. In the case of the Barb’ara, it gets its damage from your skill damage buffs, making it perfect for those who are running skill builds.

This grenade has the ability Tentacles, which causes it to create a tentacle explosion on impact. The explosion created by this impact deals skill damage. These tentacles will spawn two additional grenades that create more tentacles, also dealing skill damage.

Since every Vault Hunter in the game can run a skill build, this is a great grenade to have whenever you decide to switch up your build. You can farm this grenade from Crazed Earl in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

Sometimes you just want to fire a rocket launcher and let it delete your problems. In this case, the problem is usually a group of enemies or a massive boss that is blocking your path. The Loiter Sploiter is designed to take care of these problems quickly, and is great if you have an ordnance-focused build and amp gear.

The Loiter Sploiter’s ability, Sploiter, makes it so this weapon fires high-damage rockets. These rockets then spawn additional rockets when they explode, causing massive amounts of damage.

If you are running gear with the amped ability, this will power up these rockets, making them capable of one-shotting bosses with ease. You can get this weapon Infamous Dave in the Murders & Acquisitions DLC.

There are some grenades in Borderlands 4 that don’t just explode. Instead, they have some quirky effects such as shooting lasers or a machine gun at enemies before they explode. Either way, you get an explosion.

The Alignment is one of those grenades, as it has the ability Coordinated, which makes it so the grenade seeks out an enemy when thrown, hovers above them, shoots them with a beam of elemental energy, and then divebombs them.

It is an interesting effect that makes that weapon great for dealing elemental status effects, and therefore, is good for those who want an elemental status effect build. You can obtain this grenade from the Warped & Weird Vault Card.

Speaking of the weird and quirky, the Heimdahl is perhaps the weirdest of the ordnance weapons in Borderlands 4. This is because the weapon shoots Dahl soldier heads that attack enemies. They are out for revenge, and will kill anyone in their way.

The ability of this weapon is called Rig. It fires soldier heads that fly around the battlefield, track down enemies, and vomit on them. This deals significant damage, and is a weapon that you can fire and forget since it tracks enemies.

This weapon is perfect for Vault Hunter builds where you don’t need to worry about ordnance ammo, as you can just keep firing it and clear out a room in no time. You can obtain this weapon from Captain Willis in The Maelstrom in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of legendary assault rifles in Borderlands 4, and we will show you how to get them all.

The Blockbuster grenade is one that will clear an area with ease, but you better make sure to stay out of the area or you will get killed. This grenade is designed to do one thing, which is to cause numerous explosions.

The ability of this grenade is called Got You Covered, and it does give you plenty of cover. This ability makes the grenade split into four grenades on impact. These grenades then spawn an additional two grenades. This sounds normal until you realize that these grenades all bounce in place, creating explosions as they do.

It will cover the field in explosions, and you just need to stay out of the way so you don’t get killed. You can get this grenade from Vile Lictor in Terminus Range.

The Firepot is similar to the Swarm grenade, but it focuses on dealing fire damage and it loves to stick grenades to enemies. Torgue returns with one of the finest grenades in Borderlands 4, and it packs a serious punch.

The ability of this grenade is called Spicy, and it makes the grenade spawn homing Torgue sticky grenades that attach to enemies. In total, nine grenades will spawn from this bad boy, and they will each explode after 13 seconds, igniting the enemies that are unfortunate enough to be hit by them.

It is another throw and forget style grenade that does an amazing job covering the field without you needing to focus too much on what you are doing. You can get this grenade from Leader Willem in Grindstone of the Worthy.

The Waterfall was one of my first legendary grenades in Borderlands 4, so it holds a special place in my heart, and it might be a bit weaker than some of the other weapons on this list. However, this doesn’t mean that it isn’t worth getting, as it packs a serious punch.

This grenade has the Waterfall ability, which makes it explode multiple times whenever it hits an enemy. Throw it in a group, and each enemy damaged by the grenade will cause another explosion, cascading the damage over the surrounding area.

It can wipe out groups of enemies easily, but it is noticeably not as effective as the Swarm. You can get this grenade by farming Bio-Bulkhead in the Dissected Plateau.

There are some grenades and ordnances that can clear out entire rooms, and then there are some that are focused on one thing, and that is killing bosses. The Draupner is basically a delete button for life’s problems, and it is amazing.

Return Wave is the name of the Draupner’s ability, and it makes the weapon fire out three saw blades in a horizontal pattern from the weapon. These saw blades return to you after two seconds or upon impact, effectively hitting enemies twice over.

This ordnance effectively diminishes the damage numbers of every other ordnance in the game, making it a must-have weapon. You can obtain it by running the Takedown at the Hadron Abyss.

There are plenty of legendary weapons in Borderlands 4, but these are the weapons that you should have at this point if you want a strong build.

#4362. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4360. Amazon’s Mass Effect TV Series Is Reportedly Still In Production Despite BioWare Closure

EA shut down legendary RPG developer BioWare this week, canceling its in-development fifth Mass Effect game as a result. Despite the closure, Amazon Prime’s upcoming Mass Effect streaming series will proceed as planned, according to a report by IGN.

Amazon MGM Studios began developing a Mass Effect series in 2024. At the time, Mass Effect series executive producer Mike Gamble confirmed the show isn't a retelling of the video games, saying, “The show will explore a brand-new story within the universe's timeline, and will be set after the original trilogy. It won't be a retread of Commander Shepard's story – because after all... that's YOUR story, isn’t it?”

With BioWare’s closure, one would think the series would go up in smoke, but sources within Prime Video speaking to IGN confirmed that it remains in development. Furthermore, all of the creatives involved remain so. This includes showrunners Doug Jung (The Cloverfield Paradox, Star Trek Beyond) and Daniel Casey (F9: The Fast Saga, Wardriver), former Marvel Studios head Avi Arad, and Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik. Mike Gamble was also involved, and this report suggests he still is, but it remains to be seen how his position on the project has changed with BioWare’s demise, given he served as a guiding voice from the studio. The Mass Effect series has no release window.

The Mass Effect series joins other video game adaptations Amazon has in the works, which include a third season of Fallout (with Aaron Paul joining the cast), a live-action God of War series starring Dave Bautista, a live-action Tomb Raider series starring Sophie Turner, as well as series based on Life is Strange and Wolfenstein.

#4359. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 to reach first Worlds semi-final since 2019

Invictus Gaming knocked out fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening quarter-final of Worlds 2026 in Allen, Texas. The result guarantees China a semi-final place after the LPL's 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage.

Invictus Gaming are through to the last four of Worlds 2026. They beat fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening match of the Knockout Stage. The series was played at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas, on 3 November (US time).

The win guarantees China a semi-final place. That matters after the LPL’s 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage. IG now meet either Gen.G or LYON. Gen.G beat IG 1-0 in the Swiss Stage and finished it with a perfect 3-0 record.

TES played the event without ZUIAN. On 6 October the club announced that Bai ‘369’ Jia-Hao would move into the starting line-up because of visa problems affecting ZUIAN.

The stand-in still made his mark. IG won Game 1 after building a gold lead of more than 10,000. TES levelled in Game 2 when 369, on Renekton, killed JiaQi and TheShy on his own late in the game. IG then took the next two games to close out the series.

Every Knockout Stage match is a single-elimination best-of-five played with Fearless Draft. The two sides knew each other well. They met twice in best-of-five series in September. IG won 3-2 in the LPL Split 3 playoffs on 5 September. TES won 3-1 in the LPL Regional Finals on 17 September.

The prize money gap is now fixed. Worlds 2026 has a total prize pool of US$5,000,000, with US$1,000,000 for the winner. Each losing semi-finalist receives US$400,000, so IG are guaranteed at least that sum.

IG’s run began with a mid-season rescue. The team started LPL Split 3 in the Nirvana Group. The club then asked TheShy and Rookie, who were both on a break, to come back. The pair helped the side qualify for Worlds. Both won the 2018 world title with IG.

TheShy said he had promised IG’s CEO he would help if asked. “I came back to keep my word,” he said after the series.

The semi-finals will be played in Allen on 7 and 8 November. The final will be held in Brooklyn on Saturday 14 November at 2pm EST.

#4356. Remedy Explains Control Resonant's Most Memorable, Unexpected Sequence And Its [REDACTED] Inspirations

Please allow the first sentence here to warn you that this interview discusses a portion of Control Resonant that takes place near the end of the game and is arguably the most unexpected and surprising sequence. I encourage you to experience it without spoilers. So if you haven't beaten the game yet, please do, and then come back to this page.However, if you have beaten the game, or curiosity has driven you to learn what game has been redacted from the headline and why (it's the 1995 Super Nintendo RPG, EarthBound, by the way), then please read on.

In the late-game of Control Resonant – basically right before you tackle the final confrontation – the game suddenly shifts timeframe and genre to become a 16-bit RPG. The nostalgic lens turns the game into something that feels like 1995's EarthBound, complete with turn-based battles, in order to explain the trauma that Jesse and Dylan went through at a young age after they came across an object of power: the slide projector. The whole sequence is funny, heartbreaking, weird, and importantly effective at making you feel you are seeing a part of their past. It was particularly effective on me as I have fond memories of playing EarthBound and games like it when I was young. To see and experience Dylan and Jesse's childhood this way felt accurate, as absurd as that sounds.

I reached out to Remedy to specifically discuss that portion of the game. You can find the full e-mail interview below with the team members who contributed to its creation.

The big RPG backstory sequence for Jesse and Dylan – why approach the storytelling that way?

Lead level designer, Anne-Marie Grönroos: The basis for the whole sequence is that the Hedron attacks Dylan's mind, breaks his reality apart, and he has to rebuild himself. We wanted the reality-breaking part to affect the game itself and have the player feel some of the confusion Dylan is feeling by breaking the fourth wall.

Who pitched that sequence, how did they pitch it, and was it difficult to sell to the larger team?

Grönroos: At Remedy, ideas rarely come from a single person or team, and we rarely do formal pitches, but rather discuss and workshop ideas cross-craft until they start taking the shape of something we like. The initial idea from the writer was for this to be a text-based adventure, to return to a very early form of a video game to show that the Patterning is devolving him, but an Alan Wake 2 DLC had already done that, and we wanted to find something else.

Independently, some months ago a level designer had suggested a sidequest with JRPG pixel graphics, but that had gone nowhere. I remembered that and suggested doing an old Final Fantasy-style JRPG here, which also felt more fitting since that’s the type of game Dylan and Jesse would have played in their childhood, and not a text-based adventure. People got excited about that, and after some concerns about feasibility, we went forth with it. It helped that the level designer who had originally wanted to do the JRPG side quest is a big fan of these types of games and has made them before. I wouldn’t have dropped something this crazy on someone who wasn’t passionate about it and ready to figure out how to do it with our engine that’s not built for anything like this.

Is EarthBound (Mother in Japan) the primary inspiration for that sequence? Are there big fans of those games at Remedy?

Senior level designer in charge of the JRPG quest, Arhi Makkonen:The whole Quest was born from that childhood feeling I had when playing old JRPGs – Final Fantasy, Breath of Fire, Chrono Trigger, Secret of Mana, Bahamut Lagoon, and yes, Mother. The most important thing for me was capturing that feeling of a time when games felt like magic. I think many people can relate to that nostalgia, and now Jesse and Dylan share that feeling in the game.Visually, Mother was a major inspiration of course. Juuso Anttila is the concept artist who did all the splendid pixel art for Rebuild quest. Mother's style fits the mysterious Americana small town vibe perfectly. We also couldn't pass up the pun about a story revolving around "Not-Mother" that was made in the style of Mother.

Was it difficult to implement the sequence into the game? Did Remedy's Northlight Engine need significant work to account for the sequence?

Makkonen: The Northlight engine was designed to work perfectly for third-person action games. Well, Rebuild Quest is pretty much the opposite of that. Northlight is a specialized tool rather than a general-purpose one, so we had to come up with some rather creative solutions to create a 2D JRPG.

First of all, we’re faking the 2D look. In reality, the entire JRPG Ordinary exists within a 3D world that the camera simply views from directly overhead. It occupies a tiny patch in a remote corner of the game world—a space where 3D Dylan would barely have room to stand. The entire game-within-a-game is written in Lua; our incredibly versatile game designer, Tommi Saalasti, created the underlying system, upon which I was then able to build the story.

Since we didn't really have the tools to create a game like this, I had to hand-code every single detail. Dylan takes one step up, Dylan turns left (where Jesse hopefully is at that moment), text box 1, text box 2. The Lua script for the Rebuild quest alone probably contains as many lines of code as all the other quests in the game combined. And then there were things like animations were restricted to a maximum of two frames, and some UI elements were created using static particle effects.

So yes, we faced all sorts of challenges and compromises, but at the heart of it all was a wonderful story – simply told in a somewhat unconventional way. We trusted that the narrative would make up for some of the imperfections.

Remedy has a reputation for big unexpected and often crazy singular moments. What are the conversations like around delivering those? In pre-production, are there conversations like, "What is the big moment for this one?" Or do they happen pretty naturally?

Grönroos: They both happen naturally and we also have conversations about what the big moments should be. Sometimes we like a section so much that we decide to put even more resources and importance to it, even if it wasn’t supposed to be all that important from the get-go. The Into the Sinkhole quest, for instance, is a quest that wasn’t planned to be a “tentpole moment” from the start, but we kept putting more effort into it when it was shaping up to be something very special.

But most setpieces in the game were planned to be such from the early stages of pre-production. In Resonant, we wanted to have multiple standout moments instead of a single sequence like the Ashtray Maze overshadowing everything else, and I’m happy to see that players have different favorites.

And a different approach from Control is that several of these memorable moments (Sinkhole, Underpass Fault, the JRPG section) are more emotional and subdued instead of bombastic action (although we also have big action setpieces), which was an interesting challenge itself.

Was there a fear that the visuals would limit the emotional impact of the sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, but we decided to trust the writing. Several other games have managed to deliver a similar emotional impact despite pixel graphics (and sometimes because of them, since the level [of] abstraction can make characters more relatable and up to the player’s interpretation), so we weren’t too concerned.

Was there a fear that action game fans would be frustrated by the RPG sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, this was the main concern about the sequence. It was a very polarizing sequence in the playtests: people either loved or hated it. We did discuss shortening it significantly, but in the end decided to keep it as it is but added some fast travel options and make some parts skippable. There were more fans than haters, and we didn’t want to sacrifice something we really enjoyed.

How concerned were you about the actual RPG mechanics of that sequence?

Makkonen: Since Rebuild doesn't feature a vast number of battles, we didn't need to build particularly deep RPG or progression systems. The combat served as an additional storytelling tool – illustrating how bullies torment Dylan, showing his first fight (against rats, naturally), and depicting his eventual abduction by the FBC.

Refining the combat to be simple, yet offer the player meaningful choices required a few iterations. In addition to standard attacks, the children can occasionally use special abilities: Dylan delivers a heavy blow to a single enemy, while Jesse fires at everyone. Enemies deal enough damage that defending becomes necessary when multiple foes target the same character.

The lightbulbs in The Underpass mission goes in similarly unexpected, animated directions. How did that mission come about? What was the pitch like for that one?

Grönroos: That one started with the idea of doing something comically mundane, switching lightbulbs, and adding a paranatural twist to it. The cartoon man wasn’t in the initial version, but instead we were going to do live action videos and have Dylan get stuck in that video as the end twist. They were supposed to be old-fashioned “work safety” videos explaining how to change lightbulbs, and as the quest went on, it became more and more obvious that the maintenance guy in the videos was too aware of what Dylan was doing. This all came out from a one-hour workshop.

There wasn’t really a pitch, but rather a back-and-forth like “could we do a quest about Dylan changing lightbulbs in a ritualistic way? We could have these sentient work safety videos explain how to do it and “Dylan could get trapped inside the video.” Much later, when the live action turned out to be a no-go, we pivoted to the current cartoon instead, and that was even funnier than our initial idea.

#4355. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

#4353. 10 Pokémon You Could Take in a Fight

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Have you ever thought about the various types of Pokémon out there? There are some that are quite terrifying. After all, some of them are sharks, others are literal dragons, and there are even Pokémon gods.

Living in the world of Pokémon, you need to be able to defend yourself, and instead of using another Pokémon to fight your battles, you need to start throwing hands. So, I pose the question, “What Pokémon do you think you could take in a fist fight?”

Do you think you are able to beat up an Eevee? Maybe you could take down an Arcanine. Here are some Pokémon you would definitely stand a chance against.

Hear me out, but I think we could all easily take a Ditto in a fight. It has the ability Transform, but in battle, it only transforms into what it is currently fighting. Therefore, the Ditto would transform into you.

Do you think you could take yourself in a fight? I certainly think I could take myself in a fight. It wouldn’t be the easiest battle, but it is certainly better than dealing with a fox that can breathe fire or a mouse that can electrocute you.

You know your strengths and weaknesses, and so all you really need to do is use that to your advantage. Ditto doesn’t know anything about your weaknesses, so you have an advantage.

If it wasn’t obvious, Komala is based on the Koala Bear, and its Pokédex entries make it out to be one in the same. It eats poison leaves that only it can digest. This makes it tired, and it continuously sleeps.

It is said that Komala is asleep from the time it is born to when it dies, and that all of its movements are based on dreams that it is having. This makes it a prime target, and a Pokémon that you could easily take in a fight.

The only issue you may have while fighting this Pokémon is that it will thrash about wildly if you remove the log it is holding. Just don’t mess with its log and you will be fine. It will just think the fight was a dream.

Spoink is an adorable little Pokémon that nobody would ever hurt, but if it came at you looking to fight, you could easily take it. Its Pokédex reveals your entire plan of action, as it states that it needs to keep bouncing in order for its heart to keep beating.

All you need to do is knock it over. It might give you some trouble with its bouncing, but if you can get ahold of its tail, all you need to do is get its back to the ground and its heart will stop.

That is pretty grim, but you have to remember that it is survival of the fittest out there, and Spoink is one of those Pokémon that can easily be defeated with little prep time and some strong actions.

Pokemon isn't all about types and stats. With the right strategy and a bit of training, any Pokemon can be a force to be reckoned with.

Slowpoke is constantly the butt of the joke when it comes to the Pokémon being slow. Its reaction timing is so poor that you could probably land 20 punches before it even realizes what is going on.

Think about it. In the games, people eat Slowpoke tails. It is so common that there are even restaurants in Lumiose City that sell it for dinner every night.

I can only take that as a sign that Slowpoke is easily defeated and captured. How else would they be able to get so many of those tails? After all, you wouldn’t be able to do the same to a Pokémon like Totodile. It would immediately bite your face off.

Sudowoodo would be a terrifying Pokémon to fight, but its pre-evolution, Bonsly, would be an easy victory. Bonsly isn’t much of a fighter, preferring to rest for hours in arid climates.

Enemies don’t typically attack Bonsly because it exudes moisture from its eyes that look like tears. However, we can see through this deception, and that makes us a difficult foe for this Pokémon.

It is said that Bonsly can easily be defeated if it gets too wet, so all you really need to do is dump a bucket of water on it and it is done for. You just need to have no empathy while dealing with this Pokémon or you won’t be able to finish the job.

Some Pokémon are tiny and have barely any defense mechanisms. One such Pokémon is Caterpie. While it may be a cute bug, it is also a bug that you could easily take in a fight.

The only real issue here is that it has a defense mechanism that allows it to release a horrifically foul odor from its body, but if you bring some nose plugs, you will be perfectly fine. Maybe fight it while wearing a gas mask just to be safe.

Other than that, you don’t have to worry about anything from this Pokémon. It has a massive appetite for leaves, so all you really need to do is wait for it to start eating and jump it. Everything will be fine unless you are afraid of them like Misty is.

Milcery is a strange Pokémon, as its body is literally cream. Its Pokédex entry says that it is born from “sweet-smelling particles.” These particles condense into a cream that forms Milcery’s body.

Well, if Milcery is made of cream, that means you just need to eat your way to victory. That sounds like a simple victory to me.

The Pokédex entries give an idea about how this Pokémon fights. It says that Milcery just covers attackers in cream and runs away. In other words, find a way not to get blinded by cream, and you will have no problem taking this Pokémon out. You will even have desert for later.

This list covers the worst Pokémon from generations 1 through 9, and why they fail to capture the attention of players.

Fidough is adorable, there is no denying that one, but it also wouldn’t be difficult to take it in a fight. All it is known for, according to the Pokédex, is producing yeast with its breath to help baked goods rise.

It is also dependent on humans. One of the Pokédex entries says that it has been protected by humans for generations, so it probably doesn’t know how to defend itself without the help of a human companion.

Plus, its short and stubby legs are a bit of a disadvantage. This is a fight that you could easily win. Now, it might be a completely different conversation when Dachsbun is involved, but luckily, we are just talking about Fidough here.

You might see me calling Magikarp weak and pathetic and think that I am just being cruel, but believe me, I am only following what the Pokédex says. Some of the early Pokédex entries say that Magikarp is a weak and pathetic Pokémon that only flops about.

Magikarp is known for getting easily pushed around. It may have some tough scales, but all you need to do is bring a slightly strong weapon and you are golden. Maybe a few kicks would be enough.

During the fight, it will only splash about. Just watch for when it hits seven feet in the air, because that is the height limit for it. You may think the water would save it, but there are so many of them, you are bound to catch one easily.

There are some very weak Pokémon in the games and anime. For instance, Wishiwashi is very weak in its solo form, but I don’t feel like fishing for hours or jumping into the water. However, Sunkern doesn’t have that issue and it is also one of the weakest Pokémon in the game.

With 30 points in each stat and a base stat total of 180, it is amazing that Sunkern can even survive a single battle against any Pokémon. To further show how weak it is, its Pokédex entry says that it tries to move as little as possible to conserve energy.

With how little Sunkern likes to move and how weak it is, I bet anyone could take it in a fight. I’d be shocked if anyone lost to this Pokémon.

From Ultra Necrozma’s stat boosts to Volo’s grueling final battle, these Pokémon encounters bend the rules to deliver memorable challenges.

#4351. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

We’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.

#4349. Dragonheir tier list - Characters ranked by elemental type

The only correct way to compare characters is through their elements. We have ranked each of them on the Dragonheir tier list.

Updated on November 7th, 2026 - Version: 0.335.194360  - Added: Cia (The Weeping Nun), Celestine, Cyanos (The Librarian), Riviel (The Bloodspike), Holfast (The Carping Scholar), Fyrenzur (The Fire Wielder), Amalfriede (The Impure), Longbeau (The Duke), Tallyn (The Fort Commander)

Also, keep in mind that these rankings will change with every season as new characters will be released. So, make sure to check back to this page to get the latest Dragonheir tier list!

Poison type characters are all about stacking poison on their enemies and causing them to take damage over time (DoT). Thanks to their immunities, Poison types are considered the best for clearing dungeons.

Ergander is arguably the star of this specific type. He's a tank that has the ability to restore his health and deal solid damage. On top of that, he can taunt enemies and become undead for a period of time. He has a very wide area of effect.

Ice type characters are characterised by their ability to apply the unique debuff Frost. When attacking an enemy with Frozen status, many Ice-type characters get extra effects, such as dealing extra damage. They are well-balanced and able to perform in PvP as well as PvE modes. A very good choice overall for new players.

Hvitar's ability to cull enemies below 15% health is extremely helpful against every opponent, regardless of their faction.

Auster is a damage carry that doesn't need a particular setup. Due to synergies in this game, many characters need a certain number of allies to boost their damage. Auster can do damage without assistance.

As we mentioned above, Vidimir has a good synergy with Dorkuraz. Voresh can potentially be used in PvP thanks to his healing ability. Pargu also sees some play in PvP, but you shouldn't invest too much in these characters.

In PvP, Tamar is an S-Tier support, better than Fungal-Glow. The problem is that he's not as effective in other modes. Ivellios, Sutha and Schaltar are Nastjenka's crew. Schaltar is easy to get since he's of Epic rarity.

Mithrasea is by far the strongest support Light-type character in the game. She can raise her fallen allies and also remove enemy buffs. Her passive can also negate fatal damage. Acilia can remove every debuff from your team and provide debuff immunity. She also has a healing ability, even though it's not that much, it all helps, right? She's amazing against bosses and certain dungeons.

Huberg is the damage carry of this type. He doesn't need much setup in order to perform. You should invest in him if you have him. Thelendor is another DPS, but simply not as good as Huberg. Lorentheel is a buffer that can raise the ATK of your whole team. Donella is an excellent support overall. He has the ability to apply crowd control to enemies (CC) and various debuffs. Hegiio is a very solid DPS character that you can use since he's of Epic rarity. His damage output is pretty solid.

Fire types damage is mainly single-target. Their special "Wild" mechanic makes their damage output even higher. They are potentially as strong as the Electric type when it comes to boss fights. Flora is the star of Fire-types. She has a lot of single-target damage and damage over time, but she also has the unique ability to release a fireball when the "Wild" special is activated. She also has a good leader skill that increases ATK by 30%. Khrysos is the Fire-type tank. He can shield and heal himself, but he's also able to negate enemy shields. He is especially good during boss fights. Felicity is a damage carry with the ability to ignore enemy shields. Definitely a character worth investing in. If you have her on your team, then Tonalnan becomes borderline S-Tier. Their synergy is really that good. Keep in mind that Tonanlnan is of Epic rarity. Errich has probably the best AoE damage on any Fire-type. Those are all of the characters ranked by their element on our Dragonheir tier list. #4348. Gen.G sweep LYON to end North America’s Worlds 2026 run and set up iG semi-final

Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.

LYON are eliminated from #Worlds2026. pic.twitter.com/y5cWOL9e5K

— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 5, 2026

The Grand Final is listed for 14:00 EST on 14 November. British fans will have a dedicated place to watch it. The British Esports Federation is holding a watch party at the new British Arena in Sunderland. It is the venue’s first esports watch party.

The arena covers 15,000 sq ft. It has a 17-metre-wide LED screen, a 200-seat viewing area and a bar. Students can get discounted tickets.

Whether Gen.G or iG make it to that final will be settled in Allen on Saturday. The Sunderland watch party runs from 5:30pm on the day of the final until 1:00am on 15 November.
